national.title: Carney looks to China as Trump tariffs squeeze Canada's car industry
national.summary: The PM has suggested Chinese automakers could replace American ones in Canada - but some say that would not be easy.
national.body:
Canada's car industry has become one of the clearest stress tests for Ottawa as it grapples with US tariffs on the sector.

Now Prime Minister Mark Carney has signalled that he is looking to China, where he is on a visit for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit (Apec), as part of the solution.

But that avenue is not without controversy, and is once again drawing the ire of those close to Donald Trump.

While in Cambodia earlier this week, Carney told reporters that Canada could turn to European and Asian carmakers to save its auto manufacturing sector if a trade deal with the US could not be reached.

If Canadian auto workers are "not fully utilised in a North American context, that provides other opportunities.

He went on to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in China on Tuesday for their second head-to-head in less than a year. The two talked of the importance of developing their relations, and Carney said they had agreed to further tariff cuts.

Neither side mentioned vehicles specifically, though analysts suggest the issue will have been prominent in their minds.

In January, Carney said that opening the door to China's electric vehicles , external (EVs) could result in investment into Canadian-owned companies and the creation of manufacturing jobs in the sector.

national.title: Iran fires at U.S. facility in Bahrain as Tehran resumes strikes on Arab neighbors
national.summary: The move on Tuesday was Iran's third attack on American military targets in the kingdom in recent days as Tehran resumed strikes on its Arab neighbors after a two-month lull.
national.body:
David Rising, Associated Press David Rising, Associated Press

Amir-Hussein Radjy, Associated Press Amir-Hussein Radjy, Associated Press

CAIRO (AP) — Iran fired drones on Tuesday at a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain, its third attack in recent days on American military targets in the tiny island kingdom in the Persian Gulf after a roughly two-month lull in fighting.

After issuing an alert about the incoming fire, Bahrain said that its air defense systems had successfully intercepted the "treacherous Iranian aerial attacks."

The U.S. military said there was no damage to U.S. equipment or injury to American personnel.

The attacks have brought condemnations from the region, while analysts say that Tehran's growing economic pressures and stalled peace negotiations are raising the risk of renewed escalation.

Iran has been suffering under a naval blockade that the U.S. has enforced on it for months in and around the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for the world's energy supplies where Iran and its proxies have disrupted shipping since the war began Feb. 28.

U.S. President Donald Trump has been circumspect on his next steps for the Iran war, now in its eighth month despite an initial promise it would last only a matter of weeks. He has said new strikes are highly unlikely, but he has also sent a third aircraft carrier and thousands more troops to the Middle East — and told Vice President JD Vance that talks aren't needed at this time.

national.title: NSA's classified internal network goes down, sources say
national.summary: Two U.S. officials tell CBS News that so far there is no evidence of a cyberattack.
national.body: Washington â The National Security Agency's internal network used to store and share classified information went offline Tuesday, according to multiple U.S. officials familiar with the situation, prompting the agency to stagger arrival times for some personnel at its headquarters at Fort Meade, Maryland.The network, dubbed "NSA Net," is used for classified communications and information sharing within the nation's largest intelligence agency.A U.S. official told CBS News that the NSA experienced a "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance." The official continued that "while some internal systems were affected, mission/critical capabilities remain fully operational and our ability to defend National Security continues." The official said that NSA's infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events.Two U.S. officials told CBS News that, at this point, there is no evidence the disruption was caused by a cyberattack. Multiple sources told CBS News that the agency was seeking to avoid having large numbers of employees log on to their computers simultaneously while the network was experiencing problems, which is why they decided to stagger arrivals. Sources referred to this as "Code Gray," part of a modified reporting schedule.Sources familiar with Fort Meade's operations said the installation remains under normal operating conditions, with gates and campus-wide services unaffected. The sources explained that the NSA operates within its own secured campus and can establish unique reporting requirements for its personnel, independent of the larger installation.In the meantime, some activities are being redirected to other NSA facilities around the country, according to sources familiar with the situation.It was not immediately clear how long the network had been offline or when full service might be restored. national.title: Retail spending slowed in October as high prices gave shoppers pause
national.summary: Shoppers increased spending more slowly in October as economic uncertainty and high prices led more Americans to pull back on a variety of purchases.
national.body:
Anne D'Innocenzio, Associated Press Anne D'Innocenzio, Associated Press

NEW YORK (AP) — Shoppers increased spending more slowly in October as economic uncertainty and high prices led more Americans to pull back on a variety of purchases from cars to clothing and furniture, even their hobbies, ahead of the unofficial start to the holiday shopping season.

Retail sales rose 0.2% in October, down from a 0.8% gain in September, according to the Commerce Department's report released Tuesday.

Sales at gas stations rose 1.5% last month after spiking 30.3% in September. Excluding gas stations, retail sales rose just 0.1%.

Overall retail sales were pulled down by a decline in sales at motor vehicle and parts dealers. Motor vehicles and parts dealers had a 1.6% drop in sales in October, reversing a 1.3% increase in September. Excluding auto-related stores, retail sales rose 0.6%.

Adjusting for higher prices, consumer spending was "negative," according to Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, according to data released last week, hotter than expected.

"The cautious consumer is back," Long wrote Tuesday. "October retail sales were tepid. Budgets are tight for many households."

She noted the drop in gas prices in November will help free up some much-needed cash this holiday season, but middle-class and moderate-income households are "feeling the strain."

national.title: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
national.summary: It marks the first sanctions since the UK announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
national.body:
The UK has sanctioned companies it said are involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.

The government said the sanctions against eight construction and property development firms would disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support building in the West Bank.

The construction of settlements, which are illegal under international law, has risen sharply in recent years. Settler attacks on Palestinians and their property have also surged.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the sanctions a "hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies".

Criticising the move on X, he wrote that Israel - as it has done in the past - will respond with "countermeasures", and that "decisions will be announced in due course".

"Israel will not bow to external pressure or change its policies as a result," Saar said, adding that they will "consider new ways to strengthen Jewish communities" in the West Bank, and "protect those involved in developing and building".

Israel previously condemned UK sanctions related to West Bank settlements, accusing the Labour government of "systematically acting against the State of Israel".

The Palestinian foreign ministry welcomed the sanctions and called on other countries to follow suit.

national.title: Jensen Huang says he would be 'honoured' to return as Nvidia CEO if board asked him
national.summary: Huang says he has had an "outpouring" of calls from investors and others calling for him to return.
national.body:
Jensen Huang said he would be "honoured" to return as the boss of tech giant Nvidia if the board asked him to, in his first public comments since his shock resignation.

"I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely," Huang said on X, days after reports he had extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy.

He said he had an "outpouring" of calls from company employees, investors and others calling for him to return as CEO of Nvidia.

But, as the BBC reported on Monday, Nvidia's board is not considering bringing him back to lead the company.

The prospect of Huang returning at this point looks unlikely.

The company's board is investigating his conduct , which includes an alleged affair with an Nvidia executive.

The AI chip giant is set to report its financial results later on Tuesday, during which the company's interim chief executive, Collette Kress, may address the situation with Huang.

Beyond the internal Nvidia investigation, Huang's affair with a woman suspected of being an asset for Beijing is set to see the billionaire questioned before multiple committees of US lawmakers in the weeks ahead.

national.title: Debunking social media posts that claim a 90-day blackout will start Nov. 17
national.summary: Americans don't need to stockpile for widespread disruptions to power, water and food supplies, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said.
national.body:
A 90-day nationwide blackout is not looming for the U.S., despite social media call outs to prepare for such a doomsday scenario.

Stand with free and independent journalism. Join Press Pass from PBS News

Multiple TikTok posts say the blackout will start Nov. 17 and warn people to stock up with food and other supplies.

A Nov. 14 TikTok post went even farther, showing President Donald Trump purportedly saying the blackout is coming.

"A 90-day blackout is going to happen before the end of the year," Trump appears to say from the White House press briefing room.

That video was manipulated. PolitiFact found the original video of Trump talking Nov. 9 in the press briefing room; he didn't announce a 90-day blackout. Among many things, he talked about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and the Iran war. The TikTok account that posted the video uses the purported clip to promote buying cryptocurrency before the supposed blackout and has posted other manipulated videos of Trump.

Fact-checkers at Snopes also found similar manipulated videos of Trump shared on Facebook and Instagram promoting cryptocurrency and claiming that it would make people money during the "upcoming" blackout.

A Spanish-language TikTok post said the blackout already started, pointing to the Nov. 12 to 14 Microsoft outage and the Federal Aviation Administration's Nov. 13 order to ground all flights because of faulty old equipment. Microsoft said in a Nov. 13 X post the outage was a technical issue, not a cyber attack, and the FAA allowed flights to resume Nov. 13.

national.title: U.S. identifies remains of 6 soldiers killed in Korean War, including teens
national.summary: The identifications are part of an ongoing effort to locate and identify the remains of U.S. soldiers killed in the Korean War.
national.body: Six soldiers who died in the Korean War, including two teenagers, have been accounted for decades after their deaths, the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency announced Monday.The identifications are part of an ongoing effort to locate and identify the remains of those killed in the Korean War. When a soldier is marked as accounted for, they receive a burial with full military honors.U.S. Army Cpl. Jackie Lee Thurman was a member of Battery B, 99th Field Artillery Battalion, 1st Cavalry Division. Thurman, 18, was a forward observer near Waegwan, South Korea, when his post came under heavy attack, according to the agency, and was last seen trying to evacuate a shell-shocked officer from the area while under heavy enemy fire.Afterward, Thurman was reported missing in action. A presumptive finding of death was issued on Dec. 31, 1953. His remains were declared unrecoverable two years later, in January 1956.The agency said that a set of remains, designated X-5814 Tanggok, was recovered by the Quartermaster Graves Registration Company near Kumhwa-dong, South Korea, in October 1952. The remains were interred as unknowns at the National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific in Honolulu, Hawaii. In November 2022, the agency disinterred the remains. Analysis allowed the agency's scientists to identify the remains as Thurman's. He was marked as accounted for by the agency on May 18, 2026. U.S. Army 1st Lt. Raymond Banker Gilbert was a member of B Battery, 503rd Field Artillery Battalion, 2nd Infantry Division, who was reported missing during the battle of the Ch'ongch'on River in North Korea, according to the agency. Witness statements allowed the Army to determine that Gilbert, 23, had been taken as a prisoner of war by the Chinese People's Volunteer Army and died from battlefield wounds in a POW camp on Jan. 31, 1951.After the war, a recovered set of remains was returned to U.S. custody as part of a 1954 exchange known as Operation Glory, the agency said. The remains could not be identified at the time and were buried as an unknown at the National Memorial Cemetery of the Pacific. They were disinterred on July 1, 2024, and sent to the agency's laboratory. Analysis, circumstantial and historical evidence allowed the agency to identify the remains as Gilbert's. national.title: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
national.summary: Tehran rejects any suggestion it was plotting a so-called dirty bomb attack on the US capital as "baseless".
national.body:
President Donald Trump has said the US is taking "very seriously" the potential for any Iranian plot to attack Washington DC, after he was asked about a CNN report citing US intelligence assessments.

In the Philippines, where he attended the Asean Summit, Trump nodded when asked by a journalist about the report that Tehran was planning to detonate a so-called dirty bomb in the US capital and said: "We're looking into it."

CNN cited unnamed US intelligence officials suggesting Iran could target senior figures in Trump's administration with such an attack.

Iran called the claim "baseless." Concerns about dirty bombs grew after the 9/11 attacks in 2001, although no such attack has ever occurred.

Such a device would contain radioactive material - such as uranium - which would be scattered through the air when its conventional explosive detonated.

During his comments to reporters in Manila, Trump was asked whether there was reason to believe an attack was imminent.

"I hope it's not," he said, "but we take it very seriously because they [the Iranians] happen to be crazy."

In a statement before Trump's comments, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis wrote: "We remain vigilant monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland."

national.title: Huang says he'd be "honored" to return to Nvidia as he agrees to testify to Congress
national.summary: The former Nvidia CEO's comments come as some in Silicon Valley have tried to argue that Huang was pushed out of the company too quickly amid a swirl of national security scandals.
national.body:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said Tuesday he would return to lead the company he cofounded if Nvidia's board of directors allowed him to. Huang also agreed to appear before Congress to answer questions about the national security scandals swirling around the company.

"I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret," wrote Huang in a statement posted on social media . "I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation."

Technology Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid alleged spy scandal Huang stepped down from the company last week after acknowledging that he had been unfaithful to his wife. News reports have tied him to a woman who U.S. intelligence officials say was recruited by China's spy agency , as well as with another woman who is an executive at Nvidia. NPR has not independently confirmed those reports.

Huang said he would be "honored" to return to the company if Nvidia's board agreed. His comments come as some in Silicon Valley have tried to argue that Huang was pushed out of the company too quickly, and circulated a petition to "stand with Jensen."

"We don't want rushes to judgment. We don't want political pressure from the left or the right to force a board into action before we've even taken the time to turn over the cards and learn what was done," said Brad Gerstner, the founder and CEO of Altimeter Capital, an investor in Nvidia, at Semafor's Silicon Valley and the World conference on Monday.

Huang and Nvidia's general counsel Tim Teter will answer questions behind closed doors from the House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence Committees and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party on Dec. 1st and 2nd.

Lawmakers say they want answers about Nvidia's role in alleged chip smuggling and efforts to evade export controls meant to block China from accessing the most advanced U.S. AI chips. They will also ask Huang about his involvement with Alice Huang , who was an executive with Megaspeed , a Singapore-based company that was a major customer for Nvidia's chips. In a statement emailed to NPR, Megaspeed said it "conducts legitimate and lawful business," and that Alice Huang left the company in 2025, but that it is conducting an internal investigation.

Nvidia's board said on Tuesday it had formed a committee to oversee the company's national security policies, compliance with U.S. export controls, and risk management of global trade.

national.summary: The U.S. has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus once relegated to medical textbooks has spread — largely among the unvaccinated — at the highest rate in more than 30 years.
national.body:
Devi Shastri, Associated Press Devi Shastri, Associated Press

The U.S. has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus once relegated to medical textbooks has spread — largely among the unvaccinated — at the highest rate in more than 30 years.

Mexico also lost its measles-elimination status, following a resurgence of the virus there that included a massive outbreak in Chihuahua state. Bolivia, too, lost its status.

WATCH: 'It's close to bulletproof,' doctor says of MMR vaccine as measles cases rise

The Pan American Health Organization declaration has few practical implications and is largely symbolic, but it marks a sharp turnabout in a disease largely controlled through decades of scientific advances. It also may be seen as the beginning of an era in which diseases of the past become deadly problems for the modern world.

"Measles elimination is not a trophy that is won once and placed on a shelf," Dr. Jarbas Barbosa, PAHO's director, said at a news conference. "It is an achievement that must be safeguarded every day by closing immunity gaps and ensuring we reach every community."

PAHO expects the U.S., Bolivia and Mexico to submit plans "in the coming weeks" for how each country will go about trying to stop transmission for at least a year and regain measles elimination status, said Dr. Daniel Salas, the organization's executive manager for immunizations.

Measles has been spreading throughout the Americas since 2024. The outbreaks in North America started in close-knit Mennonite communities and have since spread to areas with low vaccination rates. Last year, Canada lost its measles-free designation for the first time since 1998.

national.body:
The alarms warning of a ballistic missile threat went off just before 23:30 on Monday in Kyiv. Moments later came the boom of explosions.

Once again, the main bridges over the broad River Dnipro that cuts through the city were the target and this time the Russian missiles hit what they wanted.

Close to one end of the Pivnichnyi (Northern) bridge there is a large crater and in the pouring rain, water now rushes through it to the river below. Chunks of tarmac and metal are scattered around.

At its broadest point, the jagged hole is about eight metres wide.

The crossing is closed to all traffic apart from the occasional fire engine or police car passing at high speed. By contrast, nearby roads are jammed with cars and trucks, forced to take long detours.

Anyone in a hurry to move around this city has to walk, or cycle, across the bridge, picking their way through the wreckage. In the miserable weather, that also means getting very wet.

Masha and her family moved to a flat next to the bridge because they had been living by a power plant that kept getting hit by Russian missiles.

Last night, she was in the kitchen of their new place when the Russians struck the bridge. She thought her windows would be blown out of their frames by the explosions.

national.title: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
national.summary: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.
national.body:
After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths.

The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months.

Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination".

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines.

The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s.

The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections.

The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness.

PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year.

national.summary: Ukraine says the missile and drone attack on the strategic bridge in the Russian-annexed Crimea took weeks to plan.
national.body:
Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.

Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge has collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort.

The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before" and that Russian President Vladimir Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack.

Elsewhere, Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - had been closed after Russia hit Ukraine's capital overnight.

The Southern bridge partially reopened on Tuesday, Klitschko said.

Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.

While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of Putin meeting the leaders of China and the US. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight.

national.body: A Chinese scientist who concealed the death of a 6-year-old girl in a gene-editing trial has been fired following a government probe, according to state media. The girl died last year after receiving experimental gene therapy to correct a non-life-threatening condition — which was not disclosed in published research, an investigation found in July. national.title: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
national.summary: One of the key symbols of Russia's occupation of Ukraine has suffered major damage after a seven-stage attack by Kyiv.
national.body:
Stretching across the Kerch Strait in the Black Sea, the Crimean Bridge was always a symbol: for Russia, a prestige project cementing its claim to sovereign Ukrainian territory, and for Ukraine, a hated piece of infrastructure emblematic of Moscow's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula.

A key section of the double-arched, 12-mile-long bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said that the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".

But eight years after its unveiling, the bridge has now become material proof of Kyiv's ability to pierce through Moscow's military defences to hit even its most treasured and protected structures.

The attack on the strategic Crimean Bridge was carried out gradually to cut across several layers of defence, Kyiv confirmed on Tuesday.

For several weeks Ukraine's Security Service and its General Staff gradually destroyed air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare assets, and other designated targets, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.

A significant strike had already been reported on 16 November , when drones hit the bridge at night. Traffic was paused briefly then reinstated, and although the arch over the road section was visibly damaged, the structure remained standing.

But that hit turned out to have been only the penultimate stage of a complex attack.

national.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
national.summary: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.
national.body:
A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says.

There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority.

According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman.

There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost.

They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control.

Local Palestinians said that the events in al-Duyuk al-Tahta on Monday night began with harassment by Israeli settlers. Children threw stones, they said, and the settlers opened fire, killing Fadda al-Fahidat, who was 72, outside her home.

According to Palestinian accounts, her son rushed to the scene in his car after hearing the news and collided with an empty Israeli settler car parked outside his family home, injuring settlers who were standing nearby. The settlers then fired more shots, they said.

The statement from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "terrorists accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it", and then "exited their vehicle with weapons and attacked and harmed the occupants of the Israeli vehicle".

national.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO agrees to testify to Congress amid affair probe
national.summary: The former Nvidia chief will appear for closed-door testimony on Dec. 1 after Republicans threatened to subpoena him.
national.body: Washington — Jensen Huang, who resigned last week as the CEO of Nvidia, agreed to answer questions from House lawmakers on Dec. 1 under the threat of a subpoena amid an investigation into his affair with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy. "The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia's role in allowing dangerous [People's Republic of China] actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal," House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast, a Florida Republican, said in a joint statement announcing the date of the hearing. Mast issued the statement with GOP Rep. John Moolenaar of Michigan, the chair of the House China Committee, and House Intelligence Committee Chair Rep. Rick Crawford of Arkansas. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter voluntarily agreed to appear before the committees on Dec. 2, the lawmakers said. "We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security," the lawmakers added. A representative for Huang declined to comment. The chairmen had given Huang until 8 p.m. Nov. 13 to respond to their request for a closed-door, transcribed interview after Thanksgiving. Negotiations for the interview continued past the deadline into this week. In a Nov. 12 letter, the lawmakers warned that "failure to cooperate with this request will result in the House Foreign Affairs Committee issuing a subpoena to compel your testimony in a format of the committee's choosing." "Other committees also reserve the right to separately issue subpoenas to compel your testimony," they wrote. Moolenaar and Crawford signed the letter with Mast. In an initial letter to Huang on Nov. 4, the lawmakers sought a briefing on Nvidia's security protocols against espionage from foreign adversaries and on his relationship with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who is not related to him. The Singapore-based data center company gained access to Nvidia's highly prized chips that are banned from export to China under U.S. law. national.title: How new US chip restrictions on South East Asia will hit China
national.summary: The new rules restrict chip exports and also access to their computing power, which China relies on heavily.
national.body:
As US President Donald Trump heads to China, his administration has renewed efforts to curb Beijing's access to advanced semiconductors.

On Monday, Washington announced new interim rules that will increase scrutiny of data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.

The move not only restricts the export of advanced chips, but also access to their computing power, which Chinese firms currently rent abroad to train artificial intelligence (AI) models.

South East Asian countries in particular have invested heavily in data centres to power their AI ambitions - and Chinese firms seeking computing power overseas have been a key market.

But now these firms will need a US government licence to buy advanced chips from Nvidia or other American chipmakers. This allows Washington to monitor if those chips are being used to serve Chinese companies, or being smuggled to China.

This poses a fresh challenge for Beijing, which has become deeply dependent on compute from abroad in the wake of US export restrictions. At least 30% of China's advanced AI computing power is projected to come from renting overseas or smuggling in 2027, according to research by the Institute for Progress , external , a US-based think-tank.

China's foreign ministry called the new rules "economic coercion" and said Beijing "will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own legitimate rights and interests".

This is also a problem for South East Asian economies where large numbers of data centres have sprung up recently. Some of the firms behind them are accused of helping China evade US export controls on advanced chips.

national.body:
Konstantin Toropin, Associated Press Konstantin Toropin, Associated Press

Farnoush Amiri, Associated Press Farnoush Amiri, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump's pick to lead the U.S. Navy acknowledged the strain of the Iran war as senators from both political parties pressed him at his confirmation hearing Tuesday about the impact of long ship deployments on sailors, drawdowns to stockpiles of advanced weapons and resources being shifted away from countering China.

Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao, a Trump loyalist and combat veteran, is seeking the permanent top civilian job during a particularly volatile time in Washington. He also faces the extra hurdle of needing a waiver from Congress, because he left active-duty service less than seven years ago.

"This war, again, I know it's a strain on our Navy," Cao told the Senate Armed Services Committee, but he insisted that "it's really set China back on their heels" to see all the military services work together.

Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat from Massachusetts, grilled Cao on the costs of the Iran war, noting that independent estimates or media reports say the naval blockade on Iranian shipping costs about $32.5 million a day and Iranian strikes on the Navy's regional headquarters in Bahrain did at least $400 million in damage.

Cao confirmed the figure for the blockade but said he could not offer a full damage assessment in Bahrain because "it's a nonpermissive area for us to go," despite telling a reporter months ago that Iran "blew the hell out of Bahrain."

national.title: Gunmen kill Costa Rican journalist who reported on drugs trade
national.summary: Rodríguez had denounced alleged links between criminal organisations and powerful figures in Costa Rica.
national.body:
A Costa Rican journalist who denounced alleged links between politicians and drug traffickers in the Central American country has been shot dead.

Police said gunmen on a motorbike ambushed Camilo Rodríguez, 50, as he was travelling in his car north of the capital, San José, on Monday afternoon.

The independent reporter earlier said he had been receiving death threats from drug trafficking gangs.

Local media reported that it was the first murder of a journalist in more than two decades in Costa Rica. It comes at a time when transnational crime gangs are increasing their presence in the country, driving up its formerly low homicide rate.

The president of the Costa Rican Journalists' Association, Yanancy Noguera, said that "all evidence so far points to the silencing of a dissenting voice in Costa Rica - a person who published information about organised crime in the country".

Rodríguez had been working as a journalist for several decades, both in radio and in print.

Most recently, he had been uploading videos to social media in which he named public figures such as judges, business people and politicians, which he alleged were corrupt or had ties to known drug traffickers.

In one of his videos, he alleged that the home of Costa Rica's President, Laura Fernández, had been constructed by a company that he said had links to a criminal gang.

The fire originated on the second floor of the building at 666 South Ave. Security camera footage of the exterior of the bar on the night of the fire shows what appears to be a person in the second-floor window as the fire ignites. A person can also be leaving Star Alley, a small park which shares a fence with Lux's backyard, about six minutes after the fire starts.

"We were hoping it wouldn't have to come to this point, where it had to go public," Laughton said. "We were hoping to just find out who it was and make the proper arrest. But we haven't been able to determine that as of yet."

Police confirmed they currently have no suspects, and are asking anyone with information to contact Crime Stoppers or the department’s major crimes unit.

"Whoever did this, obviously should not be roaming free," Laughton said. "They purposely set fire to a place that so many people care so deeply about. And not only just the space itself, but there was a cat, like there was a living creature up there, and they knew that."

Laughton also said all cameras or other security systems were destroyed in the fire, and no usable information was able to be collected from them.

The cat, Woody, survived the fire. Lux remains closed, although Laughton has set a tentative reopening date for New Year's Day.

local.title: With burnout driving turnover, local leaders gather to tackle workplace mental health
local.summary: Rochester Regional Health's Dr. Brian Watkins will be speaking about a peer support group he developed for surgeons that is now operating system-wide.
local.body:
Burnout, defined as severe mental and physical exhaustion from prolonged stress, is a significant problem for both workers and their employers.

It can lead to employee disengagement and turnover. Some research says burned-out employees are three times as likely to leave their jobs than those who are more engaged at work.

Employee and workplace mental health is the theme of a one-day professional development conference in Rochester on Nov. 18 for human resources professionals, supervisors, and organizational leaders. The event will be presented by Eleversity, a professional training division of Heritage Christian Services.

Burnout is common among health care professionals. According to the American Medical Association, roughly 42% of physicians reported at least one symptom of burnout in 2025.

Dr. Brian Watkins, chair of surgery for the eastern region at Rochester Regional Health, will be speaking at the conference about Partners in Emotional Recovery, an employee peer support program he developed four years ago.

"Who are seen to be the most resilient, stoic, you know people within medicine? I think surgeons would be up on that list," Watkins said. '

Surgeons work in a high-stakes environment, making life-and-death decisions. And sometimes a patient dies after a procedure, or the doctor faces a complaint or a lawsuit.

"That's real stuff, and stuff that needs to be able to be spoken without fear of any consequence or retribution," Watkins said.

local.title: Rochester schools reinstate competitive cheerleading
local.summary: Competitive cheerleading will be reinstated this winter in Rochester city schools – but as one unified squad across all high schools, rather than separate school teams.
local.body:
Listen • 1:09 Competitive cheerleading will be reinstated this winter in Rochester city schools — but as one unified squad across all high schools, rather than separate school teams.

The district faced public backlash after cutting funding this year. Superintendent Eric Jay Rosser announced the modified format during a school board meeting last week.

“Athletics will develop a district-wide team that brings together student athletes from across all high schools,” Rosser said. “This approach is intended to support consistent participation, coordinated training, and continued skill development."

Competitive cheer is a technical, skillful, and detail-oriented sport that involves choreographed routines with partner lifts, acrobatic tumbling, gymnastic stunts and human pyramids.

The decision to pull the sport from extracurricular offerings was in response to logistical challenges, safety concerns, and student participation, Rosser said. But critics pointed to the majority minority rosters of squads.

Participation during this past school year dropped from about 100 students at the start, to 60 students by the end of the program’s season, according to the district.

“If you’ve ever been to a cheer competition, just the diversity alone is so healthy for both sides, the rural, the suburban, and the city, and the charter [school students],” RCSD alumna Karen Iglesia of the non-profit Primetime585 said in a social media post Oct. 27. “The message we’re sending to these girls, especially these girls of color is that you’re just not worth it. You’re not worth the investment. … It’s wrong.”

Iglesia, who is an RCSD alumna and co-founder of Primetime585, which promotes youth sports and supports local athletes, called on the district in a Facebook video to keep competitive cheerleading intact.

local.body:
This past election I would say was a "once in a generation" event. The only other election as one-sided that I can remember was in 1964 when Barry Goldwater ran against Lyndon Johnson for President.

This past week was an election night to remember for Democrats, and they deserve credit for recruiting good candidates throughout the country. I suppose that some Democrats might believe that this crushing defeat for Republicans in the Congress represents a fundamental shift in our politics. Yet, I look upon it more as a vote against Trump, Trumpism, MAGA, and all that came with it.

The country realized that warrantless searches, the bashing of defenseless people by ICE, punitive tariffs, attacks on our traditional allies like Canada, and finally the military attack on Iran which resulted in the closing of the main sea artery for Mideast oil causing high energy prices--was essentially the work of one man--Donald J. Trump.

There was also a human dynamic, I believe, at work. Americans expect their Presidents to be reasonable, deliberate and undertake their duties with a sense of humility. I think President Trump's arrogance and lack of humility may have been the final straw in his undoing.

Since the country was going in the wrong direction, the only answer was to elect people to the House of Representatives and U.S. Senate who would stand up to all of this. Now, we have a branch of our government, the legislature (Congress,) elected to check the excesses of the current Executive and occupant of the White House.

I also believe that there was another issue which led to Trump's downfall and the licking that the Republicans took in the election…and that is the matter of elections themselves. Despite all of our bickering over politics, Americans remain pretty much united in believing in the sanctity of our elections. At its core, elections are the basis of our democracy.

When the Trump administration started going after our system of elections, getting the federal government and post office involved--that woke up a lot of people. It was clear that the intent of the White House was not to encourage voter participation but to suppress it.

It brought back memories of the President trying to subvert the 2020 election, the "patriots" storming the Capitol, phone calls to Georgia trying to find a few thousand more votes--all of that came into view again, and Americans were tired of it. Our system of elections works, and it should not be manipulated to help those who are in power.

The most recent Fredonia water boil order prompts the following thoughts. The October dry spell had lowered the reservoir water level so that organic matter was allowed to grow, overloading and disrupting the filtration system. When that matter clogged the system, high turbidity occurred.

Fredonia Village trustees are now faced with no options. The funds for the plan to draw down the reservoir do not exist. They cannot even meet the bill from LaBella, the engineering company they hired. Even if all the moneys and grants were in place, which they are not, it would take nearly five years to complete the hook up to Dunkirk's system.

Grants have been given to several surrounding communities. So, apply for the grants. The grants would give the village the money it needs to keep the current system running until another one is in place, so why even go to another system when the present one is already being updated?

There is but one path for the village of Fredonia to take. Start now to dredge the filtration end of the reservoir. A $5 million dollar grant would buy a lot of truckloads of dredged material.

Do partial dredging each year going forward. Deepen the reservoir while planting trees on its banks to keep soil and silt in place. And most importantly, develop a yearly maintenance plan going forward so future generations will have a clean, dependable source of water.

local.body:
It is with heavy hearts that we share that Samuel L. Drayo, Jr. peacefully passed away on November 11, 2026 at age 85.

Sam was a proud life-long resident of the Village of Fredonia. He was born December 27, 1940 in Dunkirk, NY. He graduated from the Fredonia Normal School (campus school at Old Main-kindergarten thru 8th grade) and Fredonia High School in 1958. He graduated from Syracuse University in 1962, where he earned a bachelor's degree in political science. He completed courses at the Maxwell School of Citizenship and Public Affairs. He was a 1965 graduate of Syracuse University College of Law earning a Juris Doctor degree.

Sam served two years in the U.S. Army from 1966-1968, attaining the rank of Captain. He was awarded the U.S. Army Certificate of Achievement and National Defense Service Medal. He received an honorable discharge in 1968.

In 1968, Sam joined his Dad, Samuel L. Drayo Sr., and twin brother, David C. Drayo, in his family's Fredonia law practice. Sam's son, John D. Drayo joined him in 2008 and they practiced together for many years. Sam served as Village Attorney for the Village of Fredonia for 47 years from 1969 to 2016 and Village Attorney for the Village of Brocton from 2005 to 2015.

In 1984, Sam helped organize the Northern Chautauqua County Youth Hockey Association (Dunkirk-Fredonia Steelers) and was its first President serving in that role for 8 years.

Sam was kind and had a generous nature and always found time to help others with legal and personal matters alike. He loved to laugh and had a great sense of humor. In his later years, Sam enjoyed researching, writing, and speaking about Fredonia historical and civic topics, frequently publishing pieces in The Observer. He also enjoyed traveling and made many trips to Italy with his life partner, Margaret C. Roberts.

He was a member of the Dunkirk-Fredonia Rotary Club, the Knights of Columbus, American Legion Post 59 and St. Anthony's Roman Catholic Church in Fredonia, N.Y.

Sam is survived by his loving partner, Margaret C. Roberts of Hamburg, NY (formerly Margaret C. Partridge) and his two sons, Michael (Kristie) Drayo of Phoenixville, PA and John Drayo of Fredonia, NY. He is also survived by three beloved grandchildren, Joshua Grant, Henry Drayo and Sadie Kathleen Drayo and former spouse, Susan R. (Meister) Star. He was predeceased by his twin brother, David C. Drayo who passed in 1985 and his parents, Samuel L. Drayo Sr. and Sadie (Mooradian) Drayo.

The Fredonia Board of Trustees has moved its workshops to an hour before meetings and will no longer get together every Monday.

The Monday sessions alternated between workshops and meetings. The workshops are supposed to be for general discussion of village business with the meetings centered around resolutions that get voted on. The distinction matters little in Fredonia, where trustees will vote in workshops on items that they consider pressing.

Starting Nov. 23, the Fredonia trustees will now gather every other Monday in Village Hall at 5 p.m. for a workshop. The meetings are supposed to begin at 6 p.m. -- though when previous Fredonia boards had a similar schedule, the workshops often ran long.

The change comes after a recent workshop where Trustees LeeAnn Lazarony and Tim Mulholland questioned the need to convene every week. They feel village business can be successfully conducted without doing so.

Lazarony basically said she didn't want to be tied down every Monday, as she wants more flexibility to spend time with family out of state.

local.body:
With New York’s Southern Zone regular big game firearms season opening this Saturday, hunters across Western New York are making their final preparations for deer season. But let’s be honest, each and every year -- you know who you are, not everyone has enough time to get ready.

Between demanding work schedules, sometimes working two jobs just to keep up with the cost of living, and the high taxes and expenses that come with living in New York, hunting preparations can easily get pushed to the back burner. For many, opening weekend is approaching faster than expected.

That brings up a familiar question: Have you ever wondered whether the ammunition you bought on sale 20 or 30 years ago is still viable? Is it safe to use? Will it perform the way it did when you first brought it home? Or, maybe, similarly, you’ve come across a few boxes in your dad’s gun locker after he passed away, or provided to you from the family of a friend. The ammo could be even older.

Perhaps you’re looking at your own firearm and ammunition storage collection and wondering why you bought 10 boxes of shotgun slugs when you typically use only one or two slugs each hunting season. Some years, you don’t use any at all.

It’s a familiar situation for many hunters. You're not alone. Ammunition can sit untouched for years, sometimes decades, between hunting seasons. The question is whether it has been stored properly and whether it’s still safe and reliable.

The best way to store hunting ammunition can vary by geographic location, but most scenarios require similar care. Western New York’s humid summers, cold winters and seasonal temperature swings make storage conditions especially important. Moisture, condensation and excessive heat are among the biggest enemies for ammunition. The golden rule: Keep ammunition cool, dry, protected from temperature swings and stored securely.

With rifle ammunition (centerfire hunting calibers), keep cartridges in their original factory boxes and place those boxes inside a quality, gasket-sealed ammunition container. This protects them from moisture and physical damage while preserving important caliber and lot information. A rechargeable or replaceable silica-gel desiccant can help control moisture. Avoid damp basements, unheated garages and storage areas subject to condensation.

With shotgun slugs, the same basic storage approach applies. Keep them in their original factory packaging, protected from moisture and physical damage. Pay particular attention to plastic hulls, crimps and any signs of cracking or deterioration.

entertainment.summary: Cast members Matt Damon, John Leguizamo and Samantha Morton as well as casting director John Papsidera are expected to attend the ceremony.
entertainment.body:
Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey will receive the Ensemble Performance Award at the Palm Springs International Film Festival , the Palm Springs International Film Awards announced on Tuesday.

Cast members Matt Damon , John Leguizamo and Samantha Morton , as well as casting director John Papsidera, are expected to attend the ceremony. The Film Awards will take place on Jan. 7, 2027, with the festival running from Jan. 7-18.

The Ensemble Performance Award recognizes the “casting director in alignment with the Academy’s newly established best casting award.” Previous recipients include Conclave (2025), King Richard (2022), Mary Poppins Returns (2019), Hidden Figures (2017), The Big Short (2016), The Imitation Game (2015), American Hustle (2014), Argo (2013), The Social Network (2011) and Babel (2007). Related Stories Music Ella Langley Brings Country Into The Grammys' General Field With Seven Nominations Music Grammy Nominations Snubs and Surprises: Harry Styles, Madonna, Noah Kahan Miss Top Nods as Raye, Rosalía Overperform

“ The Odyssey is one of the most ambitious films ever made, and its ensemble of performances is nothing short of extraordinary,” Festival chairman Nachhattar Singh Chandi says. “From Matt Damon’s weathered turn as the hero Odysseus, to Samantha Morton’s captivating and terrifying portrayal of Circe, to John Leguizamo’s faithful guidance as Eumaeus, these are just a few of the many performances that bring this world of antiquity to vivid, undeniable life. entertainment.title: Fingers Point to RFK Jr. as U.S. Loses Measles Elimination Status
entertainment.summary: The Health and Human Services secretary is torching the nation's reputation as the global health leader
entertainment.body:
On Tuesday, the Pan American Health Organization announced that the United States, as well as Bolivia and Mexico, had lost their measles elimination status, a situation that requires “urgent attention,” said Dr. Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, at a press conference. “Elimination must be continuously protected.”

Calling measles “probably the most contagious virus,” he said that vaccination is “the main measure to protect” against it, and that vaccination coverage must remain “very high, above 95 percent” in every community.

Amid sinking vaccination rates, the same strain of the virus has now circulated unabated in the U.S. for a year, meaning that the virus is now endemic. This determination ends America’s hard-earned measles elimination status, achieved in 2000, which had been unequivocal proof that the country was doing something right in its effort to thwart spread of the disease.

The statistics are stunning. As of November 12, according to records maintained by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, there were 5,412 cases of measles reported in 2026, spread across 46 states and the District of Columbia, and 10 deaths.

Contrast that with 2024, the final year of the Biden administration, which saw a total of 285 cases.

The U.S. is not alone in seeing a rise in cases. As The Atlantic pointed out , “In January, six other countries — including Austria, Spain, and the United Kingdom — lost their elimination status. Measles was declared endemic in Canada again last year.”

But, despite a worldwide decline in vaccinations attributed to the lost momentum of the Covid-19 pandemic and rising public-health mistrust, it’s not impossible to earn or maintain the measles elimination status conferred by regional commissions of the World Health Organization.

Cabo Verde, Mauritius, and the Seychelles did it last year, eliminating measles and rubella and becoming the “first sub-Saharan countries to attain this milestone,” according to a November 2025 WHO press release . The method was not rocket science, but increased vaccination and improved disease surveillance. entertainment.summary: The reality star is speaking out for the first time since her ex Nathan Gallagher fled Australia following a domestic violence default conviction
entertainment.body:
Almost a year after Below Deck star Nathan Gallagher was arrested for domestic abuse in Australia — and 12 weeks after the news went public — Gallagher’s former partner and cast member Gael Cameron is finally speaking out about their relationship.

Cameron broke her silence on an episode of the podcast We Need To Talk , hosted by Paul C. Brunson, where she publicly accused Gallagher of abuse for the first time and described a toxic relationship that’s left her in fear to this day.

“I know that he is not afraid to do anything to throw me under. He’s not afraid to lie… He’s always had this idea that he has ownership or control over me,” Cameron said tearfully. “I still feel that. And I am still scared of him. And that’s why I’ve not said anything, even though he’s thrown all these accusations out there.”

Gallagher and Cameron met while filming Season Nine of Below Deck: Mediterranean in 2023, both working on the superyacht’s deck team. Over three seasons, their relationship evolved from flirty co-workers to welcoming a son together last June. But this August — halfway through a season where Gallagher struggled to juggle his bosun duties and be a present father — news broke of Gallagher’s December 2025 arrest on domestic violence charges. According to Australian police, Gallagher attacked Cameron at her apartment in Sydney, resulting in his arrest on Dec. 27, 2025. During the physical altercation, Gallagher “placed both of his hands around the victim’s neck applying enough pressure which made her unable to breathe,” according to police records. He was charged with assault occasioning actual bodily harm, common assault, and intentionally choking a person without consent.

Although Gallagher previously told Rolling Stone he had proof that would clear his name, he failed to appear at a mandated court hearing in September. As a result, he was convicted by default on charges of assault. Australian authorities issued a warrant for his arrest, noting Gallagher was suspected to have fled the country. Bravo has since announced it has no plans to work with him. entertainment.title: Hayden Panettiere’s Mother Blames Brian Hickerson For Star’s Death
entertainment.summary: Lesley Vogel, mother of the late TV star, gave a fiery interview doubling down on her initial statements
entertainment.body:
While the entertainment world continues to mourn the death of Nashville and Heroes star Hayden Panettiere , her mother, Lesley Vogel, is placing blame squarely on Panettiere’s former boyfriend, Brian Hickerson .

On Monday, Vogel gave her first public interview since Panettiere’s Aug. 16 death, speaking with Inside Edition about the often estranged relationship she had with her daughter and her emotions following her death. “Sadly, she allowed Brian to reel her back in,” she said. “Hayden had clearly let Brian somehow take over many aspects of her life.” (Hickerson has denied any invovlement with Panettiere’s death and has not been charged with a crime.)

Panettiere was found in her Greenville, South Carolina home, after police responded to calls for an unresponsive woman. She was 36 years old. In a public statement provided by her representatives, her father Skip Panettiere called her an “incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.” In Sept., the Greenville County Coroner’s Office revealed her cause of death as the “toxic effects” of fentanyl and other drugs. Tests found traces of Xanax, the muscle relaxant Methocarbamol, and Quetiapine, a drug that is prescribed for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or depression, but the coroner said there were no signs of trauma or foul play. On Oct. 28, the Greenville Police Department closed their investigation, ruling Panettiere’s death as “accidental.”

Throughout her time in the spotlight, Panettiere was open about her struggles with mental health; including postpartum depression following the birth of her daughter but also anxiety and substance abuse issues tied to her early brushes with fame. She also had a publicly contentious relationship with Hickerson, who remained her on-again-off-again boyfriend until the time of her death. In 2020, she requested a restraining order against him. And in her May memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning , Panettiere described their relationship being fraught with emotional abuse and physical violence. entertainment.title: Ayumu Imazu Talks ‘musubi’ & The Belief that Music ‘Brings People Together’: Billboard Japan Monthly Interview
entertainment.summary: He chatted with Billboard Japan about the making of the song & what he envisions for the Budokan and beyond.
entertainment.body:
Singer/songwriter Ayumu Imazu spoke to Billboard Japan for its Monthly Feature interview series spotlighting artists and releases on its radar.

Imazu’s latest single “musubi,” released digitally on Oct. 2, has become the biggest hit of his career. “musubi” is a love song portraying the bonds between people through the motif of the “red string of fate.” A demo posted to TikTok in late August, when only a single verse and chorus existed, spread widely and led to an “emergency release.” The track swept the charts across streaming services immediately after it dropped and earned the ​26-year-old artist his first-ever No. 1 on Billboard Japan ’s Streaming Songs chart (dated Oct. 14, 2026), marking the biggest breakthrough of his career to date.

2026 has also been a milestone year for him — it marks the fifth anniversary of his major-label debut, he announced a partnership with SKY-HI-led BMSG in February, and in May he released CLASSIC , his first album in four years. Next up, on Jan. 31, 2027, he’ll play his first-ever headlining show at Nippon Budokan, a venue he has long named as a goal. Related Wale on Triumphant Pair of 2027 Grammy Nominations for 'Everything Is a Lot': 'I Hope It Teaches a Lot of People About Resilience' Miley Cyrus Reacts to Shared Grammy Nod With Dolly Parton: 'A Beautiful Way to Honor Her Enormous Heart' Rosalía Reacts to Her 9 Grammy Nominations: See How She Celebrated Explore Billboard See latest videos, charts and news

After pouring all of himself into CLASSIC , “musubi” emerged as Imazu circled back to the foundation of his music, which is about “bringing people together.” He chatted with Billboard Japan about the making of the song, the inspiration he’s drawn from his new environment at BMSG, and what he envisions for the Budokan and beyond.

“musubi” has been generating a huge response. When did you start working on it?

Around two months ago, in mid-August. I finished the first verse and chorus at the end of August and posted it on TikTok maybe two days after that.

The title is symbolic. “musubi” is a love song about the bonds that tie people together. Where did the idea come from?

In May​,​ I released CLASSIC , my first album in four years, and most of it was new songs I co-wrote with overseas producers. I put so much into making it that I felt pretty empty in a way afterward. I was gradually taking things in and building my energy back up while touring, and as I considered what to make next, I vaguely thought it’d be nice to do something about bringing people together, because I feel that’s the biggest purpose of making music. I started making it with that as the big goal.

“I’m very grateful this book chart exists, because it adds one more way for books to reach the world,” Asai said. “From that point of view, it’s probably not a great thing for the world at large that the Japan Booksellers’ Award winner and the No. 1 book on this chart are the same title. Jaafar Jackson will always remember having a good time around the holidays.

In fact, as the Michael star—son to Jermaine Jackson and Alejandra Genevieve Oaziaza —explained, his family finds more than one way to rock with one another during the festivities.

“It’s a lot of great music playing, there’s a lot of good food,” he exclusively told E! News at the CCA's 9th Annual Celebration of Black Cinema & Television Nov. 16. “We usually love playing some board games. Pictionary is one of our favorites. It can be loud at times, I would say, but it’s great, you know, it’s wonderful.”

Also wonderful, as Jaafar admitted, would be what’s on the table, too. “There’s always some peach cobbler, apple pie,” the 30-year-old noted. “And I usually go it first—to the dessert spread.”

Sweet treats and family gatherings aside, Jafaar—who moonwalked across theater screens earlier this year with his portrayal of his uncle Michael Jackson —is also gearing up to star in the film’s sequel. However, if you’re wondering about all the details to come, you are not alone.

“I haven’t started prepping just yet, it’s so early on—I can’t really say anything,” Jafaar shared. “It’s in the early works so we’ll see as time comes. And I don’t want to give anything away but it’s going to be a very special, incredible journey, I will say.”

But for now, Jafaar is enjoying what the man in the mirror has accomplished thus far with his role.

“It’s so much to take in,” he explained of the response. “I’ve been just overwhelmed with just so much joy and gratitude because it’s been a wonderful experience for me to see how much this film has connected with people.”

entertainment.title: How Each Music Listening Platform Is Treating AI Music (Updating)
entertainment.summary: From Bandcamp's outright ban of AI music to Spotify's "AI Personas" approach, here's how all the music platforms are dealing with the flood of AI-generated content.
entertainment.body:
One of the most pressing questions in the music industry right now is how streaming services should be treating the deluge of AI-generated music on their platforms. Should AI music be demonetized, or even removed from platforms? Should it be labeled or flagged so that users know what they are listening to? Or, for those optimistic about AI’s creative possibilities, should it all just be left alone?

It’s hard to know the exact scale of AI music on streaming services today, but what is clear is that there’s a lot of it — and the amount of it is growing fast. Deezer reports the count of daily AI track uploads at over 50% at “peak level” in June 2026, and Apple Music told Billboard in April that “more than a third” of monthly uploads were 100% AI-generated. Qobuz also noted in January that 34% of new uploads each day are AI-generated. These metrics, however, may still represent an undercount of all the material that uses AI in some part of the creative process, given partially AI generated music is much more challenging to detect. Plus, it’s impossible to determine when AI is used to write lyrics or melodies that are then recorded by human musicians, unless a user offered up their prompting history.

When considering the challenges of actually implementing regulations on streaming services, the question of what to do about AI music becomes incredibly complex. There’s a risk of false positives with AI detection tools, but requiring self-disclosure from rights holders will likely lead to outright deception at worst, or innocent omission at best, given how prevalent AI elements can be at any point in the recording process.

Still, lines are being drawn, and until some sort of consensus emerges, those lines are different at different digital service providers. To learn more about what each music listening platform is doing about AI-generated music, Billboard has compiled an updating list of each services’ policies as they articulate them.

S oundCloud bans all AI-generated content on its platform that impersonates human artists or otherwise clones their voices, and it requires that AI-generated or manipulated content complies with the same platform requirements as any other music uploaded to SoundCloud. The platform itself has said it does not use any music content to train generative AI models and would not do so any time in the future without prior consent.

In an open letter in November 2026 , SoundCloud CEO Eliah Seton wrote that the company will also be adding protections against users who use AI to spam the platform with slop, and it will beef up its defenses against streaming manipulation, a common byproduct of AI. Those who violate its policies will be blocked from the platform.

entertainment.title: “In a Very Primal Way It’s About Who We Are as Queer Men in Our 60s”: ‘THR Presents’ Q&A With ‘Tip Toe’ Star Alan Cumming and Creator Russell T Davies
entertainment.summary: The men behind the thriller series, which recently premiered on Starz, discuss their long-awaited collaboration.
entertainment.body:
“The idea rose up in me unstoppably,” says Russell T Davies of his new series Tip Toe . The creator, who was first put on the television map with his groundbreaking 1999 series Queer as Folk , had been working on another project when he found himself so increasingly alarmed by the state of the world and the cacophony of conservative and bigoted voices on the internet that he rushed home to Manchester to start writing a new script.

“I’m well known as a gay writer and activist, and when you are that person in this modern world you automatically get called a pervert online,” he explained during a recent THR Presents panel. “I get called a pedophile and a groomer daily, you can just search for my name and there it is. I’m always thinking about terrible things that might happen to me every single day.” Related Stories TV 'The Traitors' Star Ben McDonnell on 'New Blood' Set Secrets and Alan Cumming: "You Can Never Break Character" Movies 'THR Presents' Q&A With Hana Jusic, Director of Croatian Oscar Contender 'God Will Not Help'

That real-life horror became the story of Tip Toe , which follows opens with the violent hanging death of a queer bar owner at the hands of his conservative next-door neighbor and then jumps back in time to trace the seeds of the tragedy. The bar owner is played by Alan Cumming , who Davies refers to as a “sleeping giant.” Though Cumming has become known more recently for his bubbly hosting gigs on the Traitors franchise, Davies felt strongly that the actor had more to show audiences. The two first met over 20 years ago on a business lunch and have been trying to work together ever since.

“I said yes as soon as he told me about the story,” says Cumming. “I feel like it’s a fateful thing that [our working together] happened in this way, with a show that means so much to both of us. In a very primal way it’s about who we are as queer men in our 60s.”

Davies created the show with the UK’s Channel Four, and while he was ferociously writing the scripts he says he “warned” the network that they were coming. “When I eventually handed the script in to them, they commissioned the show within seven days. Nothing happens that fast. But seven days later in the middle of their Christmas dinner they said yes — that’s how much they felt it was important.”

Watch the rest of the conversation between Cumming and Davies in the video above. This edition of THR Presents is sponsored by Starz .

entertainment.title: ‘Only Murders in the Building’ Season 6 Trailer Arrives With Loads of British Stars, Cheeky Humor & Dodgy Twists
entertainment.summary: Selena Gomez, Steve Martin and Martin Short are heading across the pond to London.
entertainment.body:
It’s only murders — and British superstars — in the building. The trailer for the next season of Only Murders in the Building just dropped, featuring Selena Gomez , Martin Short and Steve Martin going across the pond to solve crimes, brushing elbows with loads of English A-listers in the process.

In the preview posted Tuesday (Nov. 17), the trio’s characters decide to travel to London to finish what their true-crime podcasting predecessor Cinda Canning (played by Tina Fey) started, attempting to solve a murder case that seemingly frames Nicola Coughlan’s character as the culprit. Suspecting her to be innocent, Gomez, Short and Martin visit the Bridgerton alum in jail, giving a sneak peek at the humor of American versus British slang that’s sure to come up a lot throughout the season.

“Are you taking the piss?” Coughlan’s character angrily asks, to which Short, as Oliver Putnam, replies earnestly: “No, I went before I left and once more before I got here.”

Perhaps the most eye-popping part of the trailer is the number of U.K. stars who make cameos in the project, from Olivia Colman to David Tennant, Martin Freeman, Jim Broadbent, Peter Capaldi, Simone Ashley, Jamie Demetriou, Richard E. Grant, Geri Halliwell-Horner, Jennifer Saunders and more. Plus, Meryl Streep returns as Loretta Durkin, who joins onscreen husband Oliver and the gang in London for the adventure.

“After successfully bringing the guilty to justice once again, Charles, Oliver and Mabel embark on their hardest case yet when the next victim — Cinda Canning — arrives at their doorstep, summoning them to London to catch her killer,” reads a synopsis for the installment, which comes with a modified title: Only Murders in London .

“Our beloved trio of true crime-solving podcasters must now navigate their way through the home of the cozy murder mystery, replete with a whole new collection of suspicious and particularly English-eccentric characters,” it continues. “But can they follow in the footsteps of the woman whose podcast started it all for them … without having their story end the same as hers?”

Gomez, who plays Mabel Mora on the show, also shared the trailer on Instagram , writing, “Our series has left the building.”

Only Murders in the Building first premiered on Hulu in 2021. Since then, it’s amassed seven Emmys across five seasons.

At the Nov. 16 event for the Netflix series—which chronicles the rise and fall of the now-incarcerated FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried and exec Caroline Ellison —Garner and Delvey shared a warm moment together on the red carpetat the Paris Theater in New York. In fact, the convicted con artist (real name Anna Sorokin ) even joined in on the question and answer segment with the Ozark alum and Altruists creator Graham Moore on stage.

Delvey, for her part, was looking as chic as ever, sporting a black skirt suit with a fitted blazer, tights and her blonde hair styled into a swoopy lob. Of course, the 35-year-old also sported a required accessory with her ankle monitor wrapped around her left leg. (Delvey is currently under a flexible house arrest from the Immigration and Customs Enforcement following her 2021 release from prison.)

Garner, for her part, matched Delvey’s color palette in a halter knee-length dress with an attached long-sleeved cover.

And while it’s been years since Garner portrayed Delvey on screen in the Netflix series, the duo’s history dates back even further to when Garner visited Delvey during her nearly four-year prison sentence following her conviction of grand larceny.

“She was very nice,” Delvey said of Garner’s visit during a 2022 appearance on the Forbidden Fruits podcast . “She came to see me and she’s a very sweet girl.”

Nevertheless, Delvey had one problem with Garner’s take on her: her iconic accent.

“It's just so weird,” she admitted, “because the way you hear yourself—like your voice is just completely different when you hear yourself on TV.”

entertainment.title: Artist-Manager Lawsuit Surge, Mavericks Name Case, Ye Litigation and More Top Music Law News
entertainment.summary: In this week's Legal Beat : Why are so many artists suing their managers? Plus, a case over The Mavericks band name, Kanye's many lawsuits, and more.
entertainment.body:
THE BIG STORY: Why does it feel like every artist is suing their manager right now?

When Timbaland filed a splashy $15 million lawsuit last month, it was the latest in a rash of such legal battles over the past year or so — including new cases from Ellie Goulding , Sara Landry , Muni Long and Andra Day and a high-profile jury trial for Chance the Rapper . They include claims of stolen money, unpaid commissions, conflicts of interest, and even an involuntarily trip to a mental health facility.

These kinds of fights have been happening for decades; the Rolling Stones , Billy Joel and Coldplay all famously battled their longtime managers. The relationship between an artist and a manager is often so intimate that the breakup can feel more like bitter divorce than a normal business dispute.

But in examining the new cases — and talking to attorneys who have litigated such cases — it quickly became clear to me that the artist-manager relationship has evolved in recent years in ways that have made it even more prone to nasty disputes. For more on why that is, go read my entire story here .

-The widow of Raul Malo, the late frontman of The Mavericks , filed a lawsuit to stop the Americana band’s remaining members from performing under that name.

-When the owners of Elvis Presley ’s music sued Suno, they joined a battle that major labels and other creatives have already been fighting for years. But as I explained here , they took different legal approach that could give artists more power to protect their identities.

-Investors in Selena Gomez ’s mental health startup Wondermind dropped their fraud lawsuit against the star and company — a case Gomez had called “absurd.”

– Summer Walker ’s longtime label/management firm LVRN countersued her for unpaid commissions and royalties, months after she accused it of skimming money from her music, touring and merch.

entertainment.title: Broadway legend Billy Porter, 57, shares major health update after terrifying illness left him on his ‘deathbed’
entertainment.summary: The actor was diagnosed with the life-threatening illness last year.
entertainment.body:
Billy Porter is feeling much better after a scary battle with sepsis left him on his deathbed last year.

In September 2025, the Broadway legend was diagnosed with sepsis, leading him to abruptly end his role in “Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club.”

“I’m great. I’m here. I’m alive,” the 57-year-old told People on Monday.

“It’s been about a year and some change since I was ill on my deathbed and the bitch is back, honey. She’s alive.”

Last spring, the “Kinky Boots” star revealed he developed urosepsis, a life-threatening reaction to an infection that begins in the urinary tract.

He claimed that the severe case left him “dead for three days.”
