entertainment.title: Cynthia Erivo Shoots for James Bond Theme During Lincoln Center Benefit Concert: ‘It’s My Dream’
entertainment.summary: The Wicked star soared during a phenomenal gala performance that found her interpreting Phil Collins, Gladys Knight and more.
entertainment.body:
Two days after stealing the show at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony, Cynthia Erivo graced the stage at New York City’s Lincoln Center on Monday (Nov. 16) for the performing arts center’s fall benefit concert. A fundraiser for the institution’s trailblazing choose-what-you-pay ticketing program (which helps make the arts accessible to all New Yorkers), the gala brought out Broadway veterans (Betsy Wolfe, Caissie Levy), fashion luminaries (Zac Posen, June Ambrose, Clint Ramos) and even the state’s Lt. Governor-Elect, Adrienne Adams.

But all eyes were on Erivo during her hour-plus concert, which found the Tony, Emmy and Grammy winner interpreting songs from Sting (“Fields of Gold”), Whitney Houston (“I Wanna Dance With Somebody (Who Loves Me)”), Bryan Adams via Brandy (“(Everything I Do) I Do It For You”) and Blood, Sweat & Tears (“I Love You More Than You’ll Ever Know”).

After owning “In the Air Tonight” at Phil Collins’ solo induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in Los Angeles on Saturday (Nov. 14), Erivo introduced her cover of the moody, percussive classic into her setlist on Monday night. She also delighted the crowd with “You First,” a relatable send-up of stubborn romance she co-wrote with South African singer Manana for her 2025 album I Forgive You.

“I sing the songs I like and you’re just along for the ride,” the Oscar-nominated Wicked star told the audience in David Geffen Hall at the top of the night. “So I always say thank you for indulging me ’cause that’s what you’re doing.” If any attendees were disappointed by the lack of tunes from the blockbuster film duology, you wouldn’t have known it by the frequent standing ovations that brought Erivo out for an unexpected swan song after she wrapped. “We didn’t have an encore planned, but we’ll figure this out together,” Erivo said just before she and her marvelous band trotted out a jaw-dropping version of “I Will Always Love You.”

But the highlight of the evening was undoubtedly her version of a hit single from another Rock Hall of Famer, Gladys Knight. Perhaps inspired by the news, confirmed earlier that day, that Robert Pattinson would step into 007’s shoes, Erivo informed the audience, “I really want to do a James Bond theme song. It’s my dream.” To make it abundantly clear that she’s more than up for the task, Erivo belted out an expressive, expansive cover of Knight’s “License to Kill” from the 1989 Bond film of the same name, bringing a stage veteran’s gift for thoughtful phrasing and a fresh creative license to the R&B ballad.

entertainment.summary: Tributes to Dolly Parton and Brooks & Dunn will be highlights of the show.
entertainment.body:
The 60th annual CMA Awards , airing Wednesday (Nov. 18) from Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, will have numerous highlights. Among them are a tribute to country legend Dolly Parton , who died in August; a tribute to Brooks & Dunn , who are receiving the Willie Nelson CMA Willie Nelson lifetime achievement award; Taylor Swift ’s first performance on the CMA Awards in 13 years; and the first-ever CMA performance by Americana stars Mumford & Sons , joined by Chris Stapleton .

The show will be hosted by Lainey Wilson for the third consecutive year. Stapleton will be busy on the night, as he’s also teaming up for a performance with Stephen Wilson Jr.

In 1978, Parton became the second woman to win the CMA Award for entertainer of the year (following Loretta Lynn). In 1988, she became the first woman to host the CMA Awards solo. In 2016, she became the first woman to receive the Willie Nelson lifetime achievement award.

Swift won the Horizon Award, now called new artist of the year, in 2007. Two years later, at 19, she became the youngest winner of entertainer of the year, a distinction she still holds. Swift is nominated this year for single of the year with “I Knew It, I Knew You,” marking her 26th career CMA nomination.

Country stars Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan and HARDY will be joined in the Brooks & Dunn tribute segment by rock stars Halestorm and Marcus King.

Presenters include many country stars as well as such more unlikely choices as pop star Michael Bublé; gospel legend CeCe Winans; actors Jessica Chastain, Glen Powell and Kimberly Williams-Paisley; and sports announcers/reporters Joe Buck and Laura Rutledge.

Clint Black, Luke Bryan and Lady A will make special appearances, along with actor/comedians Leanne Morgan and Matt Rife; and Good Morning America cohost Lara Spencer.

The 60th Annual CMA Awards will air live on Wednesday, Nov. 18 (8-11 p.m. ET) on ABC and Disney+, and will be available the next day on Hulu. The show is a production of the Country Music Association. Robert Deaton serves as executive producer, Alan Carter is director and Jon Macks is head writer.

entertainment.title: Kid Rock’s Nashville Bar Sued After Bouncers Allegedly Beat Patron Who ‘Tapped’ Guitar
entertainment.summary: A man alleges security guards at Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk & Steakhouse assaulted him after a "moment of poor judgment" last December
entertainment.body:
A Michigan man is suing Kid Rock ‘s Big Honky Tonk & Steakhouse in Nashville with claims he was beaten by bouncers at the venue last December.

Plaintiff Joshua Welch claims he was celebrating his recent college graduation with friends at the multi-level bar when he passed close to the stage and, “in a moment of poor judgment, lightly tapped the performer’s guitar with the tip of his finger.” The contact was “a light nose-tap,” his lawsuit obtained by Rolling Stone alleges, but a burly security guard quickly confronted him and started to escort him out.

“As Mr. Welch and Bouncer #1 again passed the live-music area on the way to the elevator, Mr. Welch attempted to touch the guitar a second time. At that point, Bouncer #1 became disproportionately agitated. He began pushing Mr. Welch aggressively toward the elevator,” the lawsuit, which was filed in March but only surfaced on Tuesday in a TMZ report , reads.

Welch claims two other bouncers joined in, with one allegedly slamming him against an elevator wall and pressing his arm against Welch’s neck “with significant force.” Once on the ground floor, the bouncers allegedly refused to let Welch leave and instead repeatedly shoved him to the floor, injuring his hand and finger so badly that he needed surgery, the lawsuit claims.

“Each time Mr. Welch attempted to stand up, he was forcefully shoved back down to the ground,” the filing claims. “It was as though they were using a show of force for some sick personal gratification.”

The lawsuit includes claims for assault and battery, negligence, and false imprisonment. Kid Rock, born Robert Ritchie, is not an individual defendant, only his venue. But the lawsuit claims the alleged acts “were performed by agents/employees of Kid Rock, individually and/or collectively, for the benefit of the defendant and the advancement of their business interests.”

entertainment.title: 5 Best Shows That Explore TV's Behind The Scenes Stories
entertainment.summary: From some of the greatest sitcoms ever made to gripping dramas, these shows prove that what goes on behind the scenes can be just as compelling as what's on TV.
entertainment.body:
HBO Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Ever since Dick Van Dyke and Carl Reiner took us behind the scenes of the fictional "The Alan Brady Show," we have had decades of TV shows that explore what it's like to make television. There have been sitcoms like "The Dick Van Dyke Show" and "30 Rock," dramas such as "The Curse" and "The Newsroom," and even mockumentaries like "The Comeback." The industry has been as interested in the people behind the scenes as the TV shows themselves.

With so many of these series being revolutionary in their own right, it's hard to pick the top five shows of all time. Many of these series cover different parts of the industry. "30 Rock" and "The Larry Sanders Show" are all about the comedy side of things, spoofing late-night stand up show, variety specials and sketch comedy, while the likes of "UnReal" or "The Comeback" take a look at the dark side of reality television .

This list is picking the best of the best, assessing the accuracy of each series, as well as how funny and dramatic they are in their respective genres. Above all, these are must-see TV shows that will change the way you view television.

NBC/YouTube You can't have a list about series that explore TV's behind the scene stories without " 30 Rock," one of the best workplace comedies . While it was not the first of its kind, inspired by the phenomenal "The Larry Sanders Show," it is for sure the most famous Hollywood satire sitcom. Emmy-winning showrunner and actor Tina Fey created "30 Rock" as a look into her own life as a writer on " Saturday Night Live ," back when the show was at the center of pop culture.

Fey played Liz Lemon, the showrunner of a fictional sketch series, "TGS with Tracy Jordan," who must manage the whims of her needy actors, incompetent staff, and profit-driven boss Jack (Alec Baldwin) to keep the show alive. The series was not only a look into the making of sketch comedy, but an inside scoop into TV networks too. This was mostly shown through Jack Donaghy's storylines, Liz's boss and friend who spends most of the series trying to make NBC as profitable as possible with wild ideas.

But "30 Rock" became more than just a look into behind the scenes of television. This is a time capsule of late '00s Hollywood and the industry's transformation towards embracing reality television. It's an incredibly accurate predictor of the future from serious topics like executives trying to own the rights to actors' images so they can digitally place them into shows without paying them extra money, to something as silly as a reality series about older women dating younger men. And most of all, it's really funny, with jokes that are still being referenced over a decade after it ended. If "30 Rock" is somehow not the best sitcom about making television, it's definitely up there with the best.

entertainment.title: Skydance Film Re-Org: Kira Goldberg Joins Paramount, Jesse Ehrman Upped to Run Warner Bros.
entertainment.summary: Goldberg will run Paramount‘s film operations with Don Granger, while Jesse Ehrman will run Warners, with Mikey Ireland remaining as president of production.
entertainment.body:
Skydance is sorting out its film operations at both Paramount and Warner Bros. in the wake of closing its $111 billion acquisition of Warners.

Kira Goldberg is leaving Netflix, where she was one of its top film heads, overseeing faith-based, family and young adult films for the streamer. At Paramount, she will oversee film operations with longtime Skydance executive and producer Don Granger as presidents of the motion picture group.

Jesse Ehrman , a twenty-year veteran of Warners, has been elevated to president of the motion picture group at the studio. He most recently served as president of production and development. Mikey Ireland, who joined Warners in February after being laid off at Paramount, will remain as president of production at Warners.

Warner Bros. has been without a head since Mike De Luca and Pam Abdy were fired last month amid the Skydance merger. The duo had run the studio since 2022, guiding it to a best picture win with One Battle After Another earlier this year and having celebrated hits like Sinners , A Minecraft Movie and Weapons , but seeing a number of their 2026 movies bomb at the box office, most recently the Tom Cruise feature Digger .

Elsewhere in today’s announcement was the news that Jeff Goldstein, a 48-year veteran of Warner Bros. who currently serves as the head of global distribution, will be exiting the studio, taking on a consulting role.

The execs at Warners and Paramount will all report up to Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg, who oversee all of film for Skydance. The new re-org was done with an eye toward accomplishing the 30-plus movie slate across the two studios and their various divisions, which include New Line and DC Studios, which recently ousted James Gunn and Peter Safran and will install Marvel alum Jeremy Latcham next month.

In the September settlement with California Attorney General Rob Bonta and other state AGs that cleared the path for the Warner Bros. merger, Skydance agreed that the combined studios must release 30 films for two years and then 32 for the next three years. There are penalties if this threshold isn’t met. For every movie that Skydance falls short of, the studio must pay $30 million to health and pension funds, split among the guilds. Additionally, a judge can force it to sell or spin out Miramax.

The theatrical business is central to the company’s vision for the future of Skydance. We are home to more than a century of extraordinary storytelling, legendary films and an enduring impact on audiences and culture around the world. We have both an incredible legacy to build upon and an enormous opportunity ahead of us: to champion the world’s best filmmakers, invest in ambitious storytelling and deliver an unparalleled slate of films that captivate audiences everywhere.

sports.title: NFL flexes Raiders-Browns to Sunday night in Week 12
sports.summary: Originally scheduled for SNF, Patriots-Chargers moves to 4:05 p.m. on CBS.
sports.body:
The NFL announced on Tuesday that it has flexed the Week 12 matchup between the Raiders and Browns in Cleveland to Sunday Night Football.

The two teams were originally scheduled to kick off at 1 p.m. with Patriots-Chargers scheduled for Sunday night.

New England and Los Angeles will now kick off at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. The matchup between the Titans and Jaguars in Jacksonville has also been moved to 1 p.m. on Fox.

Currently 4-6, the Raiders will have a chance to be 5-6 when they come to Cleveland as they’ll take on the Broncos in Denver this weekend. It will be Mendoza’s second career start, with the matchup against the AFC North foe in Week 12 his third.

The surprising 6-4 Browns got back in the win column with a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday. All six of Cleveland’s victories this season have come via a fourth-quarter comeback.

Cleveland and Las Vegas faced one another last season, with the Browns coming away with a 24-10 victory in Week 12. It was the first start of Shedeur Sanders’ career, though he is now serving as the backup to Deshaun Watson.

This will be the first Sunday night game in Cleveland since 2019, when the Browns fell to the Rams in Week 3.

sports.title: Brian Flores: Vikings plan to rotate players in order to deal with altitude in Mexico City
sports.summary: The 49ers are spending the week in Colorado in order to acclimate to the altitude at which their Week 11 game in Mexico City will be played.
sports.body:
But the Vikings have a plan for ensuring that their players are ready for the conditions.

“It’s a tough place to play,” Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores told reporters on Tuesday regarding the game in Mexico. “I think it’s certainly taxing, you know, I think you’re — I think as a staff, we’re already talking about, ‘Hey, we’re gonna have to rotate these guys and get, you know, everybody’s gonna have to be ready to play.’ And so, yeah, I mean, it’s certainly something that we’re going to have to deal with.

“But there’s always, you know, elements that we’re dealing with, whether it’s cold or rain or things like that. Obviously, we’re indoors, so we don’t deal with much of that. But that’s the environment we’re gonna be in. I think we prepare them to play in that environment, but I’m not gonna be silly and say, ‘Hey, everybody, hey, you’ve got to go in there for 12 straight plays.’ I mean, we’re not doing that.

“So we’ll have rotations, we’ll have a plan in place. Inevitably, we’re gonna have to fight through some of that. It’s not gonna be your average game where, you know, altitude, you just have — you literally have less oxygen. So we’ve got to do a great job as a staff of making sure — watching guys, and making sure we got guys in and out, you know, as much as we can.”

His broader message to the defense is clear: “We’re gonna need everybody.”

Regardless of the plan to rotate players, the question becomes whether the 49ers will be able to rely more heavily on their best players because they’re properly acclimated to the thinner air. The Vikings are choosing a different strategy, and it’s going to create an obvious apples to apples comparison between the approaches that the two teams have taken — especially if the 49ers players seem to be fresh and the Vikings players seem to be gassed.

sports.title: Chargers' win puts Titans in the driver's seat for the first pick in the 2027 NFL draft
sports.summary: There are no winless teams in the NFL after the Chargers won on Monday night.
sports.body:
There’s now a three-way tie for the worst record in the NFL, with the Titans, Chargers and Dolphins all at 1-8. The draft order tiebreaker goes to the team with the weakest strength of schedule, and that gives the Titans an edge.

The Titans’ 17 opponents this season currently have a cumulative winning percentage of .481, which gives them a big edge over the Chargers (whose strength of schedule is.528) and Dolphins (.588). The Titans also have a weaker strength of schedule than the 2-8 Jets and 2-7 Eagles, who are next in the draft order. If there’s a tie for the first pick, the Titans are likely to win it.

If the Titans end up with the first overall pick, the big question will be whether they believe in quarterback Cam Ward enough to use the first pick to build around him, or whether they think it’s time to draft a quarterback to replace Ward. The current betting favorite to be the first overall pick is Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. Drafting Smith would be a strong statement that the Titans are committed to putting the right players around Ward. After the Chargers’ loss on Monday, the Titans are in good shape to get that opportunity.

In the first six games of the 2026 season, wh
sports.body: Yes, the Buffalo Bills have gone from a gauntlet of high-level quarterbacks to start to the season to a consecutive collection of backups, and that drastic shift in competition has coincided with a drastic shift in defensive philosophy from Jim Leonhard. In the first six games of the 2026 season, when Buffalo’s defense was a liability, the Bills played man coverage 16.4% of the time, per Fantasy Points Data. That was the 24th-highest man-coverage rate in the NFL. Also in those first six outings, Buffalo’s blitz rate was 27.9%, the 20th-highest blitz rate in football. Then the bye week happened. Since then, the Bills’ man-coverage rate jumped to 25.7%. In that three-game sample, that’s the 13th-highest in the league. Buffalo’s blitz rate has been 33.6% combined in Weeks 8, 9, and 10, the 13th-highest blitz rate in the NFL. (Can’t forget too — there was plenty of garbage time in all three contests, where the Bills, like any team, were prompted to sit back in soft zone to keep everything in front of them.) The new man-coverage and blitz rates don’t represent massive, 180-degree changes in philosophy. And we likely won’t be able to fully discern how much Leonhard’s man-coverage and blitzing movement post-bye has actually made the Bills defense better until Thanksgiving night against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. But one thing is for sure — Leonhard’s defense has recently started to look like what we expected Leonhard’s defense to look like all along.

sports.title: All four NFC South teams are terrible at home, and one will get a home playoff game
sports.summary: The NFL's playoff seeding procedures guarantee that an NFC South team will host a playoff game.
sports.body:
All four NFC South teams are terrible at home this season: The first-place Panthers are 1-3 at home. The Buccaneers are 1-4. The Saints and Falcons are both 1-5. Add it up, and the four NFC South teams are a combined 4-17 at home.

But someone has to win the NFC South, and that “someone” will be at home during the wild card round of the playoffs, almost certainly playing some second-place team that finished the regular season with a much better record. Most likely, the NFC South winner will be the No. 4 seed, and the second-place finisher in the NFC North will be the No. 5 seed.

Currently, the NFC North features a three-way tie among the Lions, Vikings and Bears at 7-2. For those three teams, coming in second in their division and starting the playoffs on the road against the NFC South winner might actually be a better path to the Super Bowl than winning the division and starting the playoffs at home against a wild card team, likely an NFC North rival or the Rams or Seahawks.

The major prize to earn in the regular season is the No. 1 seed, which comes with a first-round bye and home-field advantage. For an NFC contender that falls short of the No. 1 seed, the best bet might be the No. 5 seed, and an easy place to play in the first round of the playoffs.

sports.title: The prediction markets are questioning Mike Vrabel's job security, again
sports.summary: During the offseason, the leading prediction markets were calling into question the future of Patriots coach Mike Vrabel.
sports.body:
Now that the Patriots have suffered a pair of embarrassing losses, the possibility of Vrabel not being the head coach of the Patriots after the season is creeping up again.

On Kalshi’s master list of coaches to be fired by March 2027 , Vrabel is at nine percent. On Polymarket, the specific question of whether Vrabel will be out by December 31, 2026 currently stands at 13 percent .

Since the regular season doesn’t end until January 10, the notion that he’s regarded as having a 13-percent chance of being fired by December 31 suggests that, if the date were shifted to Monday, January 11, the number would be higher.

Could it happen, one year after a Super Bowl berth in Vrabel’s first season with the team? The chances seem to be much lower than 13 percent, on the surface. However, there’s a weird vibe coming from the team right now, as illustrated by some of the things Vrabel said both after Sunday’s 35-10 loss to the Lions and on Monday .

It’s fair to ask whether Vrabel has lost his touch. It’s fair to wonder whether his offseason entanglement has eroded some of his authority within the locker room.

Coaches routinely rail against distractions. Vrabel created a significant one that crossed over into mainstream news. While plenty of players would likely shrug at the situation, some may see hypocrisy. Some may have become exhausted by the endless questions from family and friends about the situation.

The failure of any team in the NFL bubbles over from a complex cauldron of factors. The players may not be good enough. The preparation may not be effective enough. Bad luck plays a role.

Still, the coach needs to be able to press the buttons of the players in order to get the most out of them. And it doesn’t take much to tune someone out — even a football coach.

So, we felt comfortable with that, that he could do that. It’s another thing of actually putting the product out there and doing it, but he’s very capable. He’s got the right attitude. He’s picked things up well. He’s a smart kid.

“So, we tried to give him that 100 [rushing] yards at the end, which we normally wouldn’t do, but he was so close that I thought it was kind of a neat deal for him.”

Johnson took 22 carries on Sunday after entering the contest with 26 on the season — illustrating how he can handle an expanded workload.

That may be important moving forward, as Walker has been one of the top utilized backs in the league so far in 2026.

sports.summary: Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker failed to get a vote of confidence from head coach Brian Schottenheimer on Monday and he didn't get one from Cowboys owner Jerry Jones on Tuesday either.
sports.body:
Parker’s defense has underperformed all season and they hit another low point during Sunday’s 46-40 loss to the 49ers. The Cowboys gave up 584 yards over the course of the game and the lowlights of the unit’s performance included three touchdowns that covered at least 66 yards.

Schottenheimer said on Monday that the Cowboys were “still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand” when asked if there would be a change involving Parker. During an appearance on 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday, Schottenheimer’s comments were brought up and Jones was asked if the team is considering any changes involving Parker’s role or responsibilities heading into this week’s game against the Titans.

“We’re talking about that. I’m not going to talk about it here, but we are talking about those things ,” Jones said.

Jones gave a similar answer to a question about simplifying the defense, but having these conversations 10 weeks into the season means that there’s an acknowledgement that the status quo isn’t working. It also means that anything other than a significant shift to the team’s defensive operations is unlikely to result in the kind of change the Cowboys need to salvage their season in the final seven games.

sports.title: Through 10 weeks, the AFC playoff field is basically set
sports.summary: The 2021 expansion of the regular season to 17 games has given the bad teams more time to separate from the good teams.
sports.body:
This year, the seven AFC playoff teams have essentially declared themselves after only 10 weeks of games.

The most important developments in that regard were these: (1) the Browns beating the Texans; (2) the Ravens losing to the Chargers; and (3) the Patriots losing badly to the Lions — and losing quarterback Drake Maye, possibly for the rest of the season.

Already, we know that the Bills, Jaguars, Bengals, Broncos, and Chiefs are essentially locks to win tickets to the postseason party. The Steelers, despite being outclassed by the Bengals, have enough winnable games remaining to land a wild-card berth.

The only spot up for grabs is the seven seed. And the Browns are now in the driver’s seat.

Already, four AFC teams are dead in the water: the 2-8 Jets, the 1-8 Dolphins, the 1-8 Titans, and the 1-8 Chargers. The 3-7 Colts barely have a pulse, and it won’t last long. That’s five of 16 teams, with a fork already stuck in a spot where forks aren’t supposed to go. And the 3-6 Texans aren’t far behind.

The remaining contenders for the last spot in the playoff tree are the 6-4 Browns, the 5-5 Patriots, the 4-6 Raiders, and the 4-6 Ravens. New England could be in the process of imploding. The Raiders are 1-6 over their last seven games, and they’re now starting a rookie quarterback. The Ravens have lost five in a row.

As a result, there’s currently not much drama as to who the seven AFC playoff teams will be.

The good news is that the top of the seven-team hierarchy remains undecided — and it could stay that way for a while. The Bills, Jaguars, and Bengals stand apart from the rest. The Broncos and Chiefs remain in the mix. (The Steelers seem to be destined for another one-and-done postseason appearance, with a road game looming to Buffalo, Jacksonville, Cincinnati, or Denver/Kansas City.)

sports.title: Lions plan for Kerby Joseph to play this week
sports.summary: The Lions lost Aidan Hutchinson for the rest of the season, but they expect to have another defensive player in the lineup for the first time this year when they face the Buccaneers in Week 11.
sports.body:
Head coach Dan Campbell said on 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday that the plan is for safety Kerby Joseph to be activated from the physically unable to perform list ahead of Sunday’s game. Joseph has been practicing for the last couple of weeks and was listed as a full participant in practice last Thursday.

Joseph has been working his way back from knee issues that also limited him to six games last season. Joseph led the league with nine interceptions and was named a first-team All-Pro while playing in every game during the 2024 season.

It has been more than 13 months since Joseph has played in a game, so there will likely be some rust that needs to be knocked off once he returns to the lineup but the prospect of getting anything close to the kind of player he was prior to the injury is an appealing one for the Lions defense.

sports.title: Dan Campbell: I'm not telling players to stop celebrating because of Aidan Hutchinson's injury
sports.summary: Hutchinson tore his ACL while celebrating a sack.
sports.body:
Hutchinson will miss the rest of the season after injuring his right knee while celebrating a sack of Drake Maye in Sunday’s game. Hutchinson jumped in the air and immediately grabbed his right knee after suffering the injury when he landed back on the turf in Munich.

During an appearance on 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday, Campbell called the injury “one of those things that happened” and that “this game is built off of emotion” that he doesn’t want to take away from his players.

“I hate it, I know he hates it. But I mean, the number of moves that I’ve seen Hutch make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one leg lateral movements, lateral balances, I’m just like, it was one of those things, man,” Campbell said. “I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let’s be smart, but no, I’m not gonna say , ‘Nobody celebrates anymore.’”

Campbell recounted a story from his own playing days when he tore his biceps while celebrating a play and that didn’t lead him to make celebration avoidance a rule for the Lions when he got the job. That doesn’t make Hutchinson’s injury any easier for the Lions to deal with, but it makes his response to questions about the advice he’ll give in the future easier to understand.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills prepare to take on a divisional foe in the Miami Dolphins this week, and it will be the fourth straight game they will face a backup quarterback for at least a good portion of the game as Kyle McCord, former Syracuse and Ohio State quarterback, is set to take the first snap. Three weeks ago, MVP Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson exited the contest after one play. Two weeks back, the Bills faced Carson Wentz in a game so disastrous for the Minnesota Vikings offense, it inspired them to bring former starter Kirk Cousins back into the fold via trade from the Las Vegas Raiders. This past week, they got a heavy dose of former Clemson quarterback and rookie Cade Klubnik when New York Jets starter Geno Smith was in and out of the game. The results over these past three weeks (henceforth referred to as “the improvement period”) have been excellent for the Bills defense. The obvious caveat to any discussion here is that the results should be excellent due to the level of play challenging the Buffalo defense, but strong play against backup quarterbacks is certainly preferable to poor play against backup quarterbacks. Over this improvement period, the Bills have posted negative EPA per play each week (negative is good for defensive EPA) after only posting a negative EPA per play one time prior (week three against the hapless-thus-far-in-2026 Los Angeles Chargers offense). They also posted sub-45% success rates each week after only achieving that once before in 2026 (again, against the Chargers). It’s unquestionably the best stretch of defense the Bills have delivered so far during the regular season, and it comes not just against backup quarterbacks, but also in the three weeks immediately following the Buffalo bye week in Week 7. They’ve achieved these results through very different means. Against the Ravens, the Bills employed a blitz-heavy approach (61.3%, a season-high) with a large amount of man coverage (54.8%, also a season-high). Against the Vikings and Jets, those blitz numbers (11.8%, 31.3%) and man coverage numbers (11.8%, 16.7%) were much lower. They also achieved these results with very different run and pass success. Against the Jets, the Bills had a 37.5% pressure rate. That number is a far cry from the 61.3% pressure rate they achieved against the Ravens three weeks ago. sports.title: Report: Tests showed no major injury for Geno Smith
sports.summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith went for tests on his injured ankle on Monday, but it doesn't look like they turned up anything that will keep him from playing against the Chargers in Week 11.
sports.body:
Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that tests showed Smith avoided a major injury during the 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday. Smith left the game in the third quarter and rookie Cade Klubnik ran the offense the rest of the way.

Smith also went for a concussion evaluation during the loss, but head coach Aaron Glenn said on Monday that Smith will start this week as long as he is cleared medically.

Smith has started every game for the Jets this season. He has completed 67.1 percent of his passes for 2,226 yards, 12 touchdowns and three interceptions, but the Jets rank 26th in the league with 19.4 points per game.

sports.body: Marquise Brown is now a free agent — will the Buffalo Bills come calling? The veteran wideout was waived by the Eagles over the weekend and has now cleared waivers, making him an unrestricted free agent. Sure, the Bills are probably close to seeing Tyrell Shavers return to the field, which will make for a somewhat crowded receiver room. But this article felt necessary due to the team’s perceived past interest in Brown. Back in 2023, Sal Maiorana of the Rochester Democrat & Chronicle selected Brown as a potential trade target for the Bills at the deadline. Brown was not traded then and ended the season with 51 catches for 574 yards with four scores on 69% of Arizona’s offensive snaps. Then, after a season with the Chiefs in 2024, the Buffalo’s supposed interest in Brown was documented in a report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler in early February 2025: > “Mahomes advocated for signing Brown last year and will likely do so again. Will another star quarterback -- like Josh Allen -- be next? People with the Chiefs I spoke to this week believe that Allen has long wanted to play with Brown.” Brown ultimately re-signed with the Chiefs and had 49 catches for 587 yards and five touchdowns during the regular season last year, including a two-catch, 73-yard performance against the Bills. His yards-per-route run figure was 1.49, not tremendous but far from a totally brutal figure. If the Bills do sign Brown, it’d hardly be the first time they added a receiver after a stint as a complementary piece in Kansas City (see: Marquez-Valdes Scantling and Mecole Hardman). Brown, 29, was a first-round pick by the Ravens in 2019 and had a 1,000-yard season as a 24 year old in 2021. He was only targeted eight times in 2026 on the Eagles and had five catches for 63 yards on 20.9% of the snaps. There are plenty of charting-based metrics out there today that track how well a receiver gets open, but according to Fantasy Points Data, Browns’ average separation score of +0.053 was the highest among all Eagles receivers. Sample size certainly must be considered here, but that figure would be the third-highest average separation score among Bills receivers to date behind DJ Moore in the top spot at +0.119 and Josh Palmer at +0.118. sports.body: We have seven more games left in the Aaron Glenn era for the New York Jets. I will not remember this time period fondly whatsoever, but don’t worry, because there is a light at the end of the tunnel. ESPN’s Rich Cimini said on the “Jets Collective” podcast that he could potentially see the team making an aggressive move to trade for their next head coach. Cimini said, “The name I would watch for is KOC, Kevin O’Connell. I was just talking to a couple of people in the league today, and they said they could see [Darren] Mougey giving up a high draft pick for Kevin O’Connell. They went to college together; they have maintained a relationship. If something falls apart there in Minnesota, if they collapse down the stretch, or if they decide that they want to elevate [Brian] Flores instead of losing him to another team, maybe they make that move.” Cimini revealed that, “I was told Mougey even in meetings like offseason and preseason has spoken, internal meetings with the Jets has spoken highly of O’Connell has mentioned him in meetings and so I wouldn’t totally dismiss that. I mean, he would come in, they would get along great, they have a history, he is an offensive-minded coach with coaching experience. Now, he has made a couple of questionable quarterback decisions in Minnesota. I don’t know how much of that is him or the GM or the previous GM, but I think it’s a name to watch for; let me put that out there.” Oh baby! Spicy! Sexy! Interesting! Now I’m sure there will be a huge debate in the comment section about whether this is too crazy or even worth it. Before you run to the comments, I would just like to provide some statistical data about KOC. The Jets, in their team history, have only ever won 12 games in a regular season once (1998). O’Connell is in his fifth season as a head coach in the NFL. He has already surpassed that number twice with a 14-win season (2024) and a 13-win season (2022). Who knows if he will add a third such year to his resume; the Vikings are currently 7-2. KOC is awesome, and if the Jets can find a way, they should absolutely explore it. --- J-E-T-S! sports.title: Rams C Coleman Shelton to miss 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury
sports.summary: The Rams are on their bye this week and that gives them some extra time to figure out how to address the center position before their return to action against the Packers in Week 12.
sports.body:
Starter Coleman Shelton hurt his hamstring during Sunday’s win over the Cardinals and a team spokesperson announced on Monday night that he is expected to miss 4-6 weeks as a result of the injury. Shelton started all 10 games this season.

The Rams’ issues were compounded when Shelton’s backup Dylan McMahon also left the game. The team announced that he will be placed on injured reserve with a torn patellar tendon.

Beaux Limmer started the win over the Cardinals at guard in place of the inactive Steve Avila and moved over to center after the injuries. Bill Murray took over at guard and the Rams will hope to have Avila back when they return to the field the night before Thanksgiving.

sports.title: Jim Harbaugh on finally getting a win: "Let's do it every week"
sports.summary: Before the season, many expected the Chargers not only to get back to the playoffs for the third straight year but to finally make some noise.
sports.body:
But they roared to life on Monday night, with a win over the Ravens in Baltimore. The 23-20 victory instantly restored the boundless optimism of coach Jim Harbaugh.

“Thrilled, let’s do it every week ,” Harbaugh told reporters after the game, via Jeff Legwold of ESPN. “Good to see the smiles back on the faces.”

Harbaugh should be smiling the most. His stubborn refusal to make major changes — starting with firing or reassigning offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and continuing with a failure to trade players who won’t be there next year, like Khalil Mack — was putting Harbaugh in increasing danger of being fired. While the playoffs are a practical impossibility, Harbaugh’s obvious goal is survival for 2027.

That’s ultimately why there was no fire sale; moving good players would have made Harbaugh’s firing more likely. Surely, it’s one of the reasons why he resisted stockpiling future picks. If he’s not there to use them, who cares?

Could Harbaugh and the Chargers stack some wins? They’ve got the 2-8 Jets, the 5-5 Patriots (without quarterback Drake Maye), the 3-6 Buccaneers, and the 4-6 Raiders over the next four weeks.

It changes after that, with three of the last four games against the 8-1 49ers, the 7-2 Broncos, and the 7-2 Chiefs.

Will they run the table and sneak into the playoffs? Most likely not. Can they win enough to get Harbaugh a fourth season with the Chargers?

sports.title: Kyle Hamilton: Ravens are "disgracing" their "standards"
sports.summary: The Ravens wore all black on Monday night.
sports.body:
The Ravens’ season feels over after losing their fifth in a row, following a 4-1 start. And while it’s easy to blame the free fall on the multiple injuries suffered by quarterback Lamar Jackson, new quarterback Jacoby Brissett managed to beat the Chargers with the Cardinals in Week 1. On Monday night, the Ravens were flat, lifeless, and uninspired in prime time against the previously 0-8 Chargers.

The end result was a second straight home loss in a standalone, nationally televised game.

“Right now, we are disgracing those standards , as leaders, as players and as a team,” safety Kyle Hamilton said after the game, via Jamison Hensley of ESPN. “Whatever flak we get is warranted. . . . All the talking that’s been going on is all just talk. If you don’t go out there and do what you’re supposed to do, stop the run, nobody really cares, and stuff like this just stops mattering.”

Hamilton understands that performances like this can have consequences.

“At some point, you have to just decide about your manhood and what you want out of your job,” Hamilton said. “This is our job. We can all get fired; that’s the reality of it. If we don’t do better, then we get fired.”

Hamilton has enhanced job security from his contract. Hamilton’s $17 million salary for 2027 is already fully guaranteed. And his $17 million salary for 2028 becomes fully guaranteed in early 2027.

Still, others who lack that type of financial certainty could be facing a one-way ticket out of Baltimore.

Compounding the latest loss is the fact that it came against Jim Harbaugh, the brother of longtime Ravens coach John Harbaugh and the mentor of current Ravens coach Jesse Minter. One of the explanations for the Chargers starting 0-8 was the departure of Minter, the Chargers’ defensive coordinator during Jim Harbaugh’s first two years in L.A. and his final two years at Michigan.

sports.title: Bills and Chiefs both favored by 16.5 on Sunday, biggest point spreads of the season
sports.summary: The Bills and Chiefs are scheduled for a Thanksgiving night showdown, but before that they each have a game on Sunday.
sports.body:
The Bills are favored to beat the Dolphins by 16.5 points, and the Chiefs are favored to beat the Cardinals by 16.5 points. Those are the two biggest point spreads of this NFL season.

The previous biggest spread of this season also featured the Dolphins, when they were 13-point underdogs against the 49ers in Week 2. (The 49ers covered that spread, winning 35-13.)

The Dolphins and Cardinals are expected to be mere speed bumps on the way to one of the marquee games of this NFL season on Thanksgiving night. With the Chiefs likely to be 8-2 and the Bills likely to be 9-1 heading into that game, it has major implications for the No. 1 seed in the AFC.

sports.title: Derrick Henry on 10 carries for 10 yards: I don't have an answer, just not good enough
sports.summary: Overall, the Ravens totaled 15 carries for 16 yards, their lowest rushing output in more than 10 years.
sports.body:
Henry gained just 10 yards on 10 carries, and another 10 yards on five catches. Afterward he said he couldn’t explain what went wrong in a 23-20 loss to the Chargers.

“I don’t know. I don’t have no answer. Guys who are out there are healthy, trying to do their jobs, we just ain’t good enough,” Henry said.

Overall, the Ravens totaled 15 carries for 16 yards, their lowest rushing yardage output in more than 10 years. Henry did run for two touchdowns, but he also had five plays on which he got no gain or negative yardage. Asked if the absence of quarterback Lamar Jackson is the problem, Henry said the players who are there have to take responsibility.

“We just haven’t been executing. Of course Lamar is a big part of what we do, but it’s a grown-man league,” Henry said. “We just haven’t been doing our jobs good enough, it hasn’t been good enough, and I think losing five in a row shows that. Of course having 8 would help, but at the end of the day, we’ve got to go out there and do our jobs.”

The Ravens are 4-6 and the season appears to be slipping away, but Henry said he’ll always believe they can turn the season around.

“I’m never not gonna believe that we can turn it around and play the way we want to play,” Henry said. “You’ve still got to go to work. The season is still going to be here, you’ve still got to play. None of us are going to be like, ‘Let’s lose the rest of them.’ You’ve still got to do your best.”

sports.title: Arch Manning will participate in Senior Day, but won't comment on his future
sports.summary: Texas quarterback Arch Manning concludes his fourth slate of home games with the Longhorns on Saturday.
sports.body:
The only clue, if it even is one, comes from his decision to participate in the Texas Senior Day.

“ I’m a senior, so I’m doing it ,” Manning said, via the Associated Press.

So what’s next after he participates in the traditional farewell home game?

“I’m not really thinking about the future right now,” Manning said.

The future entails three primary options: (1) enter the draft; (2) return to Texas; or (3) transfer.

Manning started the year as the favorite to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft. That has changed.

Last year, he had 26 touchdown passes and seven interceptions for the Longhorns, who finished 10-3 for a team that did not qualify for the College Football Playoff. This year, Manning has 19 touchdown passes and 10 interceptions through 10 games. Texas currently is No. 6 in the CFP rankings.

After two straight losses (to Oklahoma and Florida), coach Steve Sarkisian didn’t rule out benching Manning.

sports.title: Monday Night Football: Chargers run past Ravens 23-20 for first win of 2026
sports.summary: The Chargers outrushed the Ravens 160 to 16.
sports.body:
By the time Brissett got the ball back, the Ravens were in need of a miracle, and his Hail Mary on the final play fell incomplete.

The Chargers won for the first time, holding off the Ravens 23-20. Los Angeles is 1-8, while Baltimore lost its fifth in a row to fall to 4-6.

The Chargers led from start to finish, winning for the first time since Week 16 of 2025 when they beat the Cowboys. They twice had a double-digit lead in the second half.

Brissett, acquired in a trade from the Cardinals last week, went 33-of-49 for 340 yards and an interception. It was his most passing yards since Week 11 of last season when he threw for 452 yards for the Cardinals against the 49ers.

He had no help from the running game, which contributed 16 yards on 15 carries. Derrick Henry had 10 yards and two touchdowns on 10 carries.

Mark Andrews caught eight passes for 82 yards and Flowers had six catches for 74 yards.

The Ravens outgained the Chargers 347 to 287, but Los Angeles gained 160 yards on the ground.

With 1:52 left, Justin Herbert completed an 11-yard pass to Charlie Kolar for a first down. The Chargers ended up punting, but the Ravens had only 11 seconds from their own 20. Brissett threw a 21-yard pass to Ja’Kobi Lane before R.J. Mickens knocked down a Hail Mary attempt intended for Lane to end the game.

sports.title: Derrick Henry's second TD has Ravens back within a FG
sports.summary: Derrick Henry has 10 carries for 10 yards, but he has two touchdowns.
sports.body:
His second one has pulled the Ravens within 23-20 of the Chargers.

The Chargers have twice had double-digit second-half leads at 20-10 and 23-13. It’s the first time the Chargers have had a double-digit lead in the second half since beating the Cowboys 34-17 in Week 16 last season. That was Los Angeles’ last win.

The Ravens, though, have made it a game despite only 15 rushing yards.

Jacoby Brissett, making his first start with the Ravens, is 25-of-39 for 280 yards and an interception.

He led the Ravens on a 10-play, 71-yard drive that has them back within a field goal.

The Ravens ruled out defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) and list right guard Vega Ioane as questionable with a left shoulder injury. Ioane played through it into the second half before Chuma Edoga replaced him.

sports.title: Rex Ryan politicks for job with Cowboys
sports.summary: Rex Ryan is plenty of things.
sports.body:
Days after being arrested for allegedly running over the feet of two people in Nashville with his pickup truck and fleeing the scene, Ryan is on the air — and he’s using the bully pulpit to politick for a job with the Cowboys.

“I could go there today and say, ‘Alright, we can have an average ass defense,’” Ryan said on ESPN New York, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing . “I’ll promise you they’d be average, I’d probably make them top-10 . But I’ll take that group right now, in one week, I’d go in and turn this thing out.”

Ryan’s pitch came after he ripped the current defensive coaching staff in Dallas.

“It’s the worst coached defense I’ve ever seen,” Ryan said. “It really is. And I’ve seen some horrible defenses, this one’s awful, and it starts with coaching. . . . They make more mental mistakes than any defense I’ve seen, as well as the physical, they’re not a tough physical defense.”

As noted separately by Michael McCarthy of Front Office Sports, Ryan also criticized the Dallas defense on ESPN’s Get Up.

“ It starts with the young guy they hired , Christian Parker,” Ryan said. “What on his resume told you he was going to be a good defensive coordinator candidate for a team like the Dallas Cowboys with Super Bowl aspirations? By the way, what told you anything about him that would make you think he could be a leader in this? Because you better hire a leader for that spot.”

(It would have been great if someone else on the show would have said, “Yeah, the Cowboys defense is extremely pedestrian.”)

“To me, absolute garbage,” Ryan said. “You can’t fire them all yet, but you damn sure better. To me, it’s the whole defensive staff. It’s not just Christian Parker. It’s not. It’s every one of those coaches on defense.”

sports.title: NFL Honors moves from Thursday back to Saturday
sports.summary: The NFL Honors ceremony is on the move, again.
sports.body:
The made-for-TV awards show, which shifts this year from broadcast to streaming, will also be sliding back to its original day.

John Ourand of Puck reports that NFL Honors will be held not on the Thursday of Super Bowl week but on the Saturday of Super Bowl weekend. The show slid to Thursday in 2022.

Netflix has acquired the rights to the show, which attracted 3.7 million viewers in February 2026.

During the event, the various Associated Press awards are announced. Also, the new class of Hall of Famers is unveiled.

As NFL programming goes, the numbers aren’t great. As live TV goes, three million people at one time is nothing to sneeze at. Whether Netflix will realize that kind of audience remains to be seen — if the official figure is even disclosed.

Regardless, the show will quickly be forgotten as the NFL pivots the next day to the biggest event of the year.

sports.title: Von Miller blames himself, not the play call, for Christian McCaffrey's late TD
sports.summary: The Cowboys pulled within 38-32 of the 49ers with 3:42 left in the fourth quarter on Sunday.
sports.body:
Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker is under fire for calling cover zero on second-and-10. He sent a six-man blitz, leaving man-to-man coverage and Von Miller matched up with McCaffrey.

The running back ran a seam route, quickly got a step (or two or three) on the 37-year-old edge rusher, caught the ball at the 40 and was off to the races. Miller reached 18.5 mph while chasing McCaffrey, but it wasn’t fast enough.

Miller, though, defended Parker and the play call on Monday.

“As a defensive coordinator in that situation, you want to be aggressive ,” Miller said, via Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . “We were trying to win the game. We were trying to create momentum. We were down by six points. If we could have just got off the field. . . . As a defensive coordinator, you want to be aggressive and want to win the game. That’s the type of mindset you want in these games.”

Parker is three years younger than Miller, but has Miller’s full support despite the struggles of the Cowboys defense. Dallas allowed 584 yards to the 49ers.

“Nah, that’s crazy,” Miller said of the calls for Parker’s job. “Christian is an incredible leader of men. All of these offensive and defensive coordinators are geniuses. Instead of me looking for a simpler way to do that job, I have to find a better way to do it. That had nothing to do with Christian Parker. I had been coached on how to play that route. I’ve had examples of that route, went over that play in practice this week. I just didn’t make that play. That had nothing to do with Christian Parker. I just didn’t execute.”

sports.title: Mike Vrabel disagrees with Milton Williams's claim that field conditions caused injuries
sports.summary: On Sunday in Germany, both teams had key players go down with significant injuries.
sports.body:
After the game, Patriots defensive tackle Milton Williams blamed the injuries suffered by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson (knee) and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (ankle) on the playing surface in Munich.

“Two top players in this league, probably got season-ending injuries playing on that [field],” Williams said, via Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald . “It was bad. But like I said, I ain’t making no excuses. [The Lions] executed. They played on the same field we did, and they executed and made more plays than we did. Give them credit.”

On Monday, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel disagreed with Williams’s opinion.

“I don’t think Drake Maye’s injury was caused by the grass,” Vrabel told reporters, “and certainly we’ve seen other players that have celebrated or have left their feet and come down and had issues at that. So the field was the same for both teams, and that’s kind of what the field was.”

Vrabel stopped short of commenting on whether the field was an issue independent of the injuries. But he’s right; it’s the same for both teams.

Still, we know by now that every field is different. And there’s surely a difference between American fields that host up to 10 games per year every year and the international one-off surfaces.

sports.title: Andy Reid: It looks like Josh Downs, Patrick Mahomes have a little connection going

sports.body:
Downs was on the field for just 11 of Kansas City’s 65 offensive snaps. But he clearly made the most of them.

“I thought Josh — for only being here for two, three days, we’d have him narrowed down to somewhere below 15-20 reps,” Reid said. “I thought, could he have had a few more? Yes. But, for what we asked him to do, he sure handled it well.

“ It looks like Pat [Mahomes] and he have a little connection thing going there , so that’s something we can build on.”

Downs’ touchdown came during a two-minute drive in the second quarter, showing the trust the club had already developed in the receiver.

“He said he felt comfortable with it, so we were able to put him in there and let him go,” Reid said. “And again, that’s a narrow package, there’s not a whole lot in that package to do. But he’s a smart kid — I’m stating the obvious here, just from our standpoint, that he was able to pick, really, the whole game plan up and handle it.

“Those are things you don’t know until you get him here, though. … You might hear it, but once you get him here, you get the reality of it.”

The Chiefs will be back home in Week 11 to face the Cardinals. We’ll see if and by how much Downs’ production increases with more time in the building.

[Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2122058091134881834?a=hfBRzB3qb8hT6ZX9EDw&s=20] Allen scored his 90th career rushing touchdown during Buffalo’s Week 10 game against the New York Jets, tying Dickerson and fellow Hall of Famer Curtis Martin for 14th on the NFL’s all-time list. He entered the game with 88. Number 89 came on a one yard run in the first quarter. Number 90 was a two-yard run on the Bills’ first possession of the third quarter. Dickerson led the NFL in rushing four times, and nobody has topped his single-season yardage record in more than 40 years. Martin opened his career with 10 straight 1,000-yard seasons, including seven with the New York Jets. Bills fans had plenty of opportunities to get tired of watching him, but now they can celebrate one of their own making what he did look average. Both finished with 90 rushing touchdowns. Allen has matched them in his ninth season while also being responsible for, you know, throwing the football. The quarterback record is already his. It has been for a while. Now Allen has reached the point where we’re comparing his touchdown total to some of the best running backs to ever play, and he could pass a few more before this season is over. One more rushing touchdown would tie Jerome Bettis and Franco Harris for 12th at 91. Barry Sanders is next at 99, followed by Marshall Faulk and Shaun Alexander at 100. Allen would need 10 more to join that pair in ninth place, which is asking a lot. But we’re talking about a quarterback with a chance to finish the season in the NFL’s top 10 for career rushing touchdowns. We can keep asking him to slide, but we shouldn’t expect that he will. Apparently, he has a few more people to catch first.

sports.body: > “I am out of carrots. I am out of sticks. Mr. Scott has time and again proven himself to be an unmanageable employee, and a poor branch manager. I recommend he be removed from that position and re-assigned to sales, where he belongs.” That quote is from a performance review of Michael Scott from the television series, The Office. Michael Scott didn’t end up losing his job as branch manager of Dunder-Mifflin in the end. Nevertheless, the review remains relatable. Sometimes people can improve their job performance, but other times you reach a realization that they just aren’t capable of doing it. We are past that stage with Aaron Glenn. We can point to any number of dubious marks of his resume as Jets head coach. He is now 5-22, sporting a worse winning percentage as an NFL head coach than Hue Jackson. Glenn now has more than twice as many double digit point losses than he has wins. The latest defeat was the ugly 31-12 blowout at the hands of the Buffalo Bills in Week 10. There isn’t much drama left surrounding Glenn. Barring an unexpected late season surge, he will not retain his job as Jets head coach for a third year. Even if there is a late season winning streak, it still might not be enough. NFL teams don’t reassign their coach to a different department. Coaching contracts aren’t written that way, and practical considerations make the sort of demotion recommended for Scott unviable. Glenn will be let go. He will make enough money to leave football if he so chooses. If he decides to continue his coaching career, he will be an in demand candidates for teams seeking a new defensive coordinator. sports.body: The New York Jets lost their fifth straight game and eighth of their last nine on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 - 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 - 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 - 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The drubbing at the hands of the Bills left the Jets with a 2-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season’s end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. The last time the Jets won more than seven games in a season Barack Obama was still President. sports.body: In the New York Jets’ 10th game of the 2026 season, on a breezy, chilly November day in East Rutherford, New Jersey, the Buffalo Bills blew out the Jets, 31 - 12. The game opened with the Jets on defense. The Bills advanced past midfield before they were forced to punt. The Jets then went nowhere and were forced to punt out of their own end zone. The Bills then went on a long, grinding drive ending in a Josh Allen quarterback sneak for a touchdown and a 7 - 0 Bills lead late in the first quarter. The first quarter ended with the score still Bills 7, Jets 0. The Jets had the ball in Bills territory. On third down and 14 the Jets did a Jets thing, throwing well short of the sticks to Mason Taylor. They settled for a short field goal to make the score 7 - 3 in favor of the Bills. Shades of last week against the Chiefs when the Jets constantly settled for field goals against a team they knew would score often against them. Trying to make the score respectable rather than trying to win. The Bills came right back with a scoring drive of their own. They narrowly missed a touchdown when James Cook dropped a perfect pass that likely would have ended in Cook scoring. Instead the Bills settled for a field goal and a 10 - 3 lead midway through the second quarter. Neither team got anything going again on offense until the Jets put together a drive featuring some nice Geno Smith to Garrett Wilson connections late in the quarter. The drive stalled inside the Bills 20 yard line and the Jets settled for another field goal with less than 20 seconds left in the half. The Jets went into the locker room trailing the Bills 10 - 6. The Jets opened the third quarter on offense. Geno Smith was on the sideline with an injury he incurred at he end of the first half. Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut at quarterback for the Jets. Klubnik put together a nice drive to open the second half, using his legs to run for a couple of first downs and finding Garrett Wilson for a long completion. Unfortunately, the drive stalled deep in Bills territory. The Jets had to again settle for a field goal, making the score Bills 10, Jets 9. The Jets momentum was fleeting.
